summary: Build customer trust by catching mistakes early. Verify picking, packing, labels, addresses, and delivery at each stage so nothing ships wrong.

title: Getting Orders Right From Start to Door
tension: Commitment to customers vs. Truthfulness about system capacity
summary: Make sure customer orders flow smoothly through your system, from promise to delivery. Balance what customers need with what you can actually do, and keep everyone in the loop.

title: Getting Paid Right
tension: Speed of payment vs. accuracy of settlement; centralised control vs. distributed verification; single-pass processing vs. iterative alignment
summary: Create feedback loops where invoices, orders, and receipts circulate together until they match perfectly, catching mistakes early and spreading problem-solving across your network.

title: Getting Paid Right
tension: Speed of payment vs. accuracy of settlement; centralised control vs. distributed verification; single-pass processing vs. iterative alignment
summary: Create feedback loops where invoices, orders, and receipts circulate together until they match perfectly, catching mistakes early and spreading problem-solving across your network.

title: Getting Paid Without Damaging Relationships
tension: Liquidity starvation vs. relationship erosion — cash must flow, but aggressive collection breaks the reciprocal bonds that enable future exchange
summary: Track unpaid invoices before they become problems, then collect them in ways that keep customers and trust intact. It's about cash flow and respect working together.

title: Getting Paychecks Right Every Time
tension: Speed of payment vs. integrity of records — the need to disburse wages reliably while maintaining the precision required by tax law, labor standards, and human trust.
summary: A reliable system that protects workers by validating pay data, preventing errors, and catching problems before money goes out. Everyone gets paid correctly, and it's auditable.

title: Getting Problems to the Right Person
tension: Speed of resolution vs. appropriate decision authority; individual empowerment vs. systemic coherence
summary: Set clear rules for when, how, and to whom problems get escalated so they're solved by someone who can actually fix them, not stuck waiting or lost in the shuffle.

title: Getting Stronger When Things Break
tension: Robustness (bouncing back to baseline) vs. Antifragility (emerging structurally stronger from stress)
summary: Build systems that improve under pressure by spreading risk, learning from small shocks, and keeping multiple options open. This transforms disruption into a source of growth.

title: Getting the Right Signal to the Right Person
tension: Centralized control vs. distributed responsiveness — how to escalate without paralyzing; how to preserve local judgment while ensuring critical signals reach authority
summary: Set clear thresholds so problems get to someone who can actually fix them, before small issues become big disasters.

title: Getting to School Safely and Fairly
tension: Algorithmic efficiency (optimizing routes, assignments, resources) vs. relational safety (embedded trust, visible care, distributed governance)
summary: Design equitable school routes and assignments that prioritize student safety and voice, while addressing how algorithms can unintentionally segregate communities.

title: Getting Your Product to People Fairly
tension: Control & Consistency vs. Adaptation & Local Autonomy
summary: Design how your product reaches customers through multiple channels that work together, with clear rules that prioritize transparency and mutual trust over extracting maximum profit.

title: Giving Animals Back the Night
tension: Human need for nighttime visibility and security vs. nocturnal species' dependence on natural darkness for navigation, breeding, feeding, and survival
summary: Map how artificial light harms nocturnal wildlife, then redesign human lighting to protect natural darkness while keeping communities safe. Darkness itself is a shared resource we need to restore.

title: Giving Marginalized Communities Real Power
tension: Paternalistic protection (policies designed FOR marginalized groups by outsiders) vs. Self-determination (policies designed BY and accountable to affected communities)
summary: Marginalized communities get binding say in city policies that affect them most, with veto power and control over enforcement. They're embedded in municipal structures to investigate discrimination and protect vulnerable groups.

title: Giving Nature a Say in Decisions
tension: Concentrated authority (elite capture, externalized costs) vs. Distributed authority (coordination overhead, slow adaptation)
summary: Share power over environmental choices across councils that represent everyone affected—people, species, ecosystems—with built-in checks to keep decisions honest and accountable to both communities and the land itself.

title: Giving Residents Real Power Over Housing
tension: Democratic legitimacy of housing decisions vs. preservation of long-term community stability and culture
summary: Communities control housing decisions that affect them—what gets built, who stays, who leaves. Residents get binding votes, not just a seat at the table.

title: Giving That Strengthens Communities
tension: Generosity as authentic flow vs. generosity as obligation; recognition-seeking vs. humble stewardship; donor control vs. recipient autonomy; short-term impulse vs. long-term systemic impact
summary: Design your giving as a practice that aligns with your values, respects boundaries, and builds lasting resilience instead of dependency. Think of it as stewardship, not rescue.

title: Govern by the Seasons
tension: Human extraction schedules vs. ecological regeneration cycles; individual access rights vs. collective recovery periods
summary: Align your decisions and access to land with nature's cycles. Use shared calendars that respect when ecosystems need rest, rotate who uses what and when, and weave reciprocal care into seasonal rhythms.

title: Governance That Grows With You
tension: Distributed voice vs. decision speed; Participation capacity vs. governance burden; Stability vs. adaptive learning
summary: Build decision-making structures that share power, develop people's skills, adapt to what's changing, and keep everyone energized for the long haul.

title: Governing Cities at the Right Scale
tension: Subsidiarity (decisions at closest scale) vs. Interdependence (flows and externalities transcend boundaries)
summary: Power works best when decisions happen close to the people affected. This pattern shows how to connect neighborhoods, districts, and city-wide efforts so nothing falls through the cracks.

title: Governing for the Living System
tension: Centralized control & external accountability vs. Distributed stewardship & commons fidelity
summary: Create accountability and decision-making structures that serve the commons itself. Design how resources flow, who gets a voice, and how the system regenerates—so it thrives beyond any single person or funder.

title: Governing Invasive Species Together
tension: Prevention and early suppression vs. acceptance of some presence and managed coexistence; centralized eradication authority vs. distributed community stewardship and negotiation
summary: When non-native species threaten ecosystems, communities can govern removal through shared decision-making, adaptive protocols, and continuous monitoring—distributing authority so local knowledge and science work together.

title: Governing Nature Across All Scales
tension: Ecological processes operate at multiple nested scales simultaneously, but governance authority is fragmented across political boundaries that ignore those scales, creating cascading misalignment where local decisions undermine landscape health and regional rules override local stewardship.
summary: Coordinate environmental decisions across local, regional, and global levels by aligning authority structures with natural boundaries and enabling seamless communication between governance layers.

title: Governing Public Companies for the Long Term
tension: Market efficiency vs. public stewardship — revenue discipline vs. universal access — operational autonomy vs. democratic accountability
summary: When the public owns a business, governance must balance making money with serving the public good. This means spreading power across multiple decision-makers, making trade-offs visible, and staying accountable to everyone.

title: Governing Water Across Boundaries
tension: Hydrological interdependence vs. jurisdictional fragmentation — water flows across administrative boundaries, but governance remains trapped within them, creating upstream-downstream conflict, externalized costs, and degraded commons.
summary: How communities at different scales work together to manage shared watersheds through nested decision-making structures that respect how water actually flows.

title: Governing Water as a Living System
tension: Extractive human demand vs. regenerative watershed health; present access vs. future generations' security; centralized control vs. distributed stewardship; market efficiency vs. commons justice.
summary: Allocate water by listening to ecological cycles and honoring Indigenous rights, through transparent institutions that protect rivers for future generations.

title: Governing Water Together Across Boundaries
tension: Political boundaries vs. hydrological boundaries — fragmented jurisdiction vs. integrated water system
summary: Design watershed governance that respects how water actually flows, shares power fairly across communities, honors indigenous knowledge, and commits everyone—present and future—to caring for the land.

title: Grazing as Nature's Weed Control
tension: Invasive species colonisation vs. native community resilience — resolved not through eradication but through competitive displacement via herbivore-mediated ecosystem engineering.
summary: Use livestock and wild herbivores to suppress invasive species and restore native plants, replacing chemicals with ecological management.

title: Green Edges That Clean Water
tension: Linear extraction (crop/pavement to waterway) vs. cyclical stewardship (nutrient capture and soil regeneration)
summary: Plant vegetated buffers between land and water to catch nutrient runoff, restore soil health, and build resilience in cities and farms.

title: Grief Gathering Spaces in Cities
tension: Private grief (isolated, pathologised, unsupported) vs. Collective grief (witnessed, ritualised, generative)
summary: Creating places where communities mourn together, remember those lost, and build lasting memorials that honor collective grief through shared rituals and care.

title: Grow Ideas Before You Organize Them
tension: Preserving generative flow vs. organizing for coherence; capturing raw insight vs. premature crystallization.
summary: Capture thoughts easily, develop them gradually, and notice when an idea feels complete. Knowledge that grows naturally, not knowledge trapped in files.

title: Growing a Living Seed Portfolio
tension: Monoculture productivity vs. polycultural resilience; genetic erosion vs. adaptive capacity; external control vs. seed autonomy.
summary: Keep diverse crop varieties alive across generations as insurance against failure, climate change, and loss of control over your food.

title: Growing and Selling Forest Abundance
tension: Livelihood extraction vs. ecosystem regeneration capacity
summary: Harvest forest products sustainably by knowing what grows, taking only what regenerates, and ensuring the people caring for the forest get paid fairly.

title: Growing Carbon Underground
tension: Visible aboveground productivity vs. hidden belowground carbon accumulation — choosing which to optimize shifts the entire trajectory of soil health and system longevity.
summary: Use healthy root systems and perennial plants to capture carbon in soil instead of annual crops. Measure what's happening beneath the surface to prove regenerative farming works.

title: Growing Civic Power at Your Own Pace
tension: Sustained civic power vs. personal depletion; meaningful contribution vs. strategic overcommitment; individual readiness vs. collective need
summary: Build participation like a garden, not a ladder. Match what you can give to what communities need, while developing skills and stamina for the long term.

title: Growing Deep Roots and Wide Branches
tension: Mastery (depth that credibly serves) vs. Adaptability (breadth that sustains through change)
summary: Build real expertise in what matters most to you, while staying curious about neighboring fields. You need both depth and range—one without the other leaves you stuck.

title: Growing Different Plants Together
tension: Monoculture efficiency vs. polyculture complexity; competitive exclusion vs. coexistence; resource concentration vs. resource distribution across time and space
summary: Design diverse species to use different resources—space, time, nutrients—so they support each other instead of competing. This makes farms and ecosystems more productive and resilient.

title: Growing Food, Building Community
tension: Global market access & standardization vs. local ecological embeddedness & cultural knowledge preservation
summary: Connect farmers directly to markets while keeping soil healthy, knowledge alive, and communities strong. Use local networks and shared decisions to balance what the world needs with what land can sustain.

title: Growing Food in Layered Forests
tension: Productivity vs. Regeneration — how to harvest abundance without degrading the living system that generates it
summary: Stack different plants at different heights to create a forest that feeds you while healing itself. Mix food, medicine, and materials the way nature does.

title: Growing Food in Layers, Year Round
tension: Maximizing food production within finite urban land vs. building resilient, self-maintaining ecological systems that improve over time
summary: Stack vegetables, fruits, and native plants across vertical space and seasons on the same land. Build soil health, wildlife habitat, and shared stewardship together.

title: Growing Food in Shared City Spaces
tension: Food security and cultural knowledge vs. land precarity and algorithmic erasure
summary: Build neighborhood food gardens with real protection and clear rules so communities can grow their own food reliably, pass gardens to the next generation, and harvest without fear.

title: Growing Food in Tree Shade
tension: Extractive management (maximize yield/timber, ignore microclimate effects) vs. Regenerative stewardship (design canopy as living climate regulator serving multiple beings)
summary: Use trees as living shade to cool soil, keep moisture in, and grow crops underneath that actually thrive. It's managing temperature and humidity as a shared resource—for plants, animals, and the soil itself.

title: Growing Food Security Through Seed Sharing
tension: Genetic resilience vs. centralized control | Adaptation to local conditions vs. monoculture vulnerability | Intergenerational continuity vs. crop extinction
summary: Communities protect their food future by stewarding seeds locally, preserving crop diversity, and building networks that keep farming knowledge and independence alive across generations.

title: Growing Food That Heals the Soil
tension: Immediate survival needs vs. long-term system health; short-term yield pressure vs. multi-generational soil building
summary: Plant multiple perennial crops together to build soil health over time, earning income while nature does the hard work of restoration.

title: Growing Food That Nourishes and Connects
tension: Industrial homogenization (yield-only selection) vs. nutritional & cultural diversity (taste, nutrients, identity as interconnected)
summary: Revive traditional crop varieties by selecting for nutrition, taste, and cultural meaning—keeping food security and community identity alive together.

title: Growing Food That Survives Together
tension: Seed as commodity (corporate control, monoculture, supply-chain fragility) vs. Seed as commons (distributed stewardship, adaptive diversity, food sovereignty)
summary: Communities preserve and share seeds as a commons, building food security through crop diversity and collective knowledge—independent from markets and governments.

title: Growing Food, Trees, and Fairness Together
tension: Short-term household income security vs. long-term ecological and carbon regeneration; individual farmer benefit vs. shared environmental outcomes
summary: Design farms that layer crops, trees, and ecosystems while sharing benefits fairly. Measure what matters—food, wildlife, carbon—and split the gains among everyone involved.

title: Growing Food Where the Sky Meets City
tension: Vertical density vs. horizontal connection; underutilized surfaces vs. carrying capacity; private asset control vs. collective stewardship
summary: Transform unused rooftops and vertical spaces into productive gardens that feed communities, with safe structures and smart growing systems.

title: Growing Food While Protecting Nature
tension: Short-term yield visibility vs. long-term adaptive capacity and genetic resilience
summary: Track how crop diversity, soil health, and wildlife affect your harvest. When you see these connections, you can grow more food while building stronger, more resilient farms.

title: Growing Forests That Care for Themselves
tension: Active tending vs. patient emergence — how to guide forest development toward desired states without imposing brittle control.
summary: Guide forests through natural growth cycles by reading where they're headed, planning for different layers to mature together, and stepping in at crucial moments to build resilience that lasts.

title: Growing Leaders at Every Level
tension: Concentrating authority in visible leaders for clarity vs. distributing it across many voices to build resilience and just governance
summary: Build leadership capacity throughout your organization so power isn't trapped with one person. Develop leaders at all levels, especially those closest to the work, so your mission survives and thrives beyond any single person.

title: Growing Life on City Rooftops
tension: Extractive capacity vs. regenerative function — using built surfaces to increase productivity without degrading the structures that support them or the living systems they host.
summary: Turn concrete and steel into working ecosystems that feed people, shelter wildlife, and cool cities down—if you design and maintain them right.

title: Growing Living Soil Together
tension: Dead soil (sealed, compacted, contaminated, biologically inert) vs. Living soil (networked, fertile, self-regulating, carbon-rich)
summary: Restore degraded urban ground into fertile, carbon-storing commons by cultivating fungi and microbes cooperatively. Transform dead dirt into self-sustaining life.

title: Growing Medicine, Protecting Nature
tension: Meeting immediate health & economic needs vs. preserving genetic diversity, population viability, and ecological regeneration capacity for future generations
summary: Build community-managed gardens that grow healing plants while protecting wild populations. Track what thrives, restore habitats, and share knowledge across generations.

title: Growing More by Growing Diverse
tension: Maximizing immediate productivity vs. building adaptive capacity and stability through living complexity
summary: Measure and nurture the web of relationships between species and ecosystem health. More diversity isn't a trade-off—it's what builds resilience and keeps systems productive over time.

title: Growing Nature's Pest Police
tension: Pest suppression as extractive chemical input vs. pest suppression as regenerative biological service requiring continuous stewardship and feedback
summary: Use predators and natural enemies to keep pests in check, then track what's working so you can adjust. It's pest control that builds itself—no chemicals needed.

title: Growing Old Together at Home
tension: Individual housing security (asset-dependent, precarious, isolating) vs. Collective stewardship (shared tenure, pooled care, embedded reciprocity)
summary: Communities where elders own their homes collectively, share caregiving, and pool resources so people can age in place with dignity and connection instead of alone.

title: Growing People Through Their Working Lives
tension: Employment security vs. continuous adaptation | Protecting accumulated expertise vs. preventing obsolescence | Stability for the person vs. resilience for the system
summary: Help workers develop skills, move forward in their careers, and transition well when circumstances change. Treat employment as a real relationship, not just a transaction.

title: Growing Regenerative Enterprises in Place
tension: Growth acceleration vs. regenerative rootedness — the pressure to scale enterprises quickly against the need for deep ecological adaptation, peer learning, and institutional maturity in specific places.
summary: How to build incubators that root new ecological enterprises in their bioregion, weave together mentors and peers, and create conditions for lasting change beyond any single person.

title: Growing Seeds, Keeping Stories
tension: Genetic erosion & monoculture standardization vs. farmer autonomy & adaptive stewardship
summary: Farmers select, breed, and document their own crop varieties, preserving genetic diversity and the knowledge tied to each plant across generations.

title: Growing Seeds That Handle Climate Change
tension: Monoculture brittleness vs. diversity complexity — the need to reduce risk through variety selection while maintaining the genetic and phenotypic diversity that enables future adaptation
summary: Build community seed libraries that test and share crop varieties proven to thrive in shifting weather. This preserves genetic diversity while helping farmers adapt.

title: Growing Seeds Together Across Communities
tension: Seed sovereignty & local adaptation vs. monoculture & genetic erosion | Decentralized stewardship vs. coordination & scale
summary: Build local networks where communities share seeds, preserve crop varieties, and keep control of what they grow—strengthening food resilience while preventing any single group from owning the seeds.

title: Growing Seeds Together, Locally
tension: Centralised seed supply (genetic homogenisation, dependency, knowledge loss) vs. Distributed stewardship (fragmentation, knowledge gaps, coordination cost)
summary: Communities collect and grow native seeds from their own land, keeping knowledge and control over what grows—preserving both the plants and the wisdom to grow them.

title: Growing Seeds Where They Belong
tension: Seed availability vs. germination conditions: Do ecosystems fail to recover because seeds are absent, unviable, or because microsites cannot receive them?
summary: Test seeds for readiness, place them in spots suited to thrive, and multiply what works. Match each seed to its best chance at success.

title: Growing Skills Before You Need Them
tension: Foresight vs. Fragility: Organizations must invest in capabilities before markets demand them, yet cannot predict which capabilities will matter. Sourcing decisions (build/buy/partner) determine whether capability becomes distributed resilience or concentrated dependency.
summary: Build capabilities as living systems, not static checklists. Develop strengths early, retire outdated skills gracefully, and decide what to build, buy, or partner for based on clear thresholds and transparent trade-offs.

title: Growing Skills Where They're Needed Most
tension: Centralized budget control vs. distributed learning agency — between fiscal accountability and adaptive capability growth
summary: Treat learning like a living resource: fund it based on real skill gaps, track what gets used, and let teams decide what they need to learn.

title: Growing Soil Health Through Compost
tension: Rapid nutrient cycling vs. stable carbon storage; maximizing decomposition speed vs. preventing contamination and immature application
summary: Turn organic waste into living soil by managing decomposition, testing maturity, and applying compost at rates your soil can actually handle.

title: Growing Soil That Fights Disease
tension: Disease prevention through external control (fungicides, sterilization) vs. disease resilience through living soil antagonism (microbial ecology, competitive exclusion)
summary: Build healthy soil ecosystems where beneficial microbes naturally suppress plant pathogens, creating lasting disease resistance without chemicals.

title: Growing Talent From Inside First
tension: Organizational continuity & knowledge retention vs. fresh perspective & adaptive capacity
summary: Move people up through open paths before hiring outside. Fair eligibility, transparent jobs, and knowledge that stays.

title: Growing the Right Crops for Your Land
tension: Maximizing yield from a single optimized variety vs. building resilience through phenological and genetic diversity that buffers against climate variability, pest pressure, and soil degradation.
summary: Choose diverse crop varieties matched to your local conditions and climate, then track how they actually perform over time. This builds your farm's ability to adapt and recover.

title: Growing the Right Customers for Your Mission
tension: Serving diverse customers with differentiated needs vs. maintaining systemic coherence, fairness, and long-term resilience across the portfolio.
summary: Figure out which customers truly align with your values and create lasting value. Then focus your energy there, adjusting as you learn what actually works.

title: Growing Through Mentoring That Lets Go
tension: Nurturing depth and trust vs. preventing enmeshment and dependency; honoring hierarchy of knowledge vs. recognizing mutual humanity across difference
summary: Build mentoring relationships where both people grow, stay themselves, and know when to part ways. How to match well, cross differences, and keep things healthy.

title: Growing Together Through Mentorship
tension: Passive reception vs. active co-creation; dependency vs. agency; extractive mentoring vs. generative lineage
summary: Mentorship works best when both people actively help each other grow. It's built on clear roles, honest reciprocity, and the expectation that mentees eventually become mentors themselves.

title: Growing Together Through Mutual Care
tension: Generic care vs. received care — the gap between what we offer and what our partners actually register as nourishment
summary: Build relationships where both sides actively help each other thrive by understanding and responding to how care is actually given and received.

title: Growing Trees That Feed Pollinators
tension: Immediate harvest needs vs. multi-generational soil and pollinator health; individual tree management vs. ecosystem-scale flowering and nesting networks
summary: Plant trees that build soil, attract pollinators, and keep producing food across generations. Design the landscape so everything works together naturally.

title: Growing Underground Networks with Fungi
tension: Visible plant health vs. invisible fungal partnership maturity — the temptation to manage what we can measure above ground while neglecting the underground network that sustains it.
summary: Partner with mycorrhizal fungi to strengthen plant health and soil. By matching the right fungi to plants and conditions, you build living networks that restore ecosystems and improve resilience.

title: Growing Ventures Together
tension: Extraction (selecting winners, hiding failure, concentrating expertise) vs. Regeneration (distributing stewardship, learning from all ventures, strengthening the whole ecosystem)
summary: Build startup ecosystems where failure is expected, success is shared, and communities benefit as much as founders. Measure what regenerates, not what extracts.

title: Growing Without Burning Out
tension: Velocity of acquisition vs. depth of rootedness; expansion ambition vs. regenerative capacity
summary: Speed up or slow down? A framework for expanding your reach while keeping roots strong and people well. Know your limits before you hit them.

title: Growing Without Burning Through Customers
tension: Growth velocity vs. Acquisition regeneration — the pressure to acquire fast without knowing if each cohort can repay its cost before degrading unit economics.
summary: Track how much you spend to win customers and how quickly they pay you back. Healthy growth means your customer base gets stronger, not weaker.

title: Growing Without Losing Your Soul
tension: Scale vs. Coherence: Growth amplifies coordination costs, dilutes culture, and distorts values—yet withdrawal forfeits impact. The tension resolves through fractal replication, not centralized expansion.
summary: How to expand your impact while maintaining core values and coherence across all levels of your organization, from individual teams to enterprise scale.

title: Growing Without Losing Your Way
tension: Speed of expansion vs. Depth of rooting; Replication of model vs. Adaptation to place; Acquisition velocity vs. Integration stewardship
summary: Expand thoughtfully by matching your growth speed to your ability to adapt. Build local roots, learn as you go, and integrate new teams as partners—not conquests.

title: Growing Your Creative Voice
tension: Individual artistic mastery vs. collective cultural continuity
summary: Build your artistic skills through practice and mentorship while passing what you learn to others. How we develop as artists and keep creative traditions alive together.

title: Growing Your Own Nitrogen With Legumes
tension: Synthetic nitrogen dependency vs. regenerative biological fixation; immediate yield certainty vs. long-cycle soil recovery; monoculture simplicity vs. polyculture complexity
summary: Partner with legumes and soil bacteria to naturally replenish nitrogen in your fields, cutting synthetic fertilizer costs while building healthier soil that lasts.

title: Growing Your Own Pest Fighters
tension: Pest suppression through external inputs (pesticides, monoculture) vs. pest suppression through living, adaptive communities (guilds of natural enemies)
summary: Design landscapes that attract and support natural predators and parasites. When bugs do the pest control work for you, it becomes free, renewable, and everyone benefits.

title: Growing Your People as a Shared Resource
tension: Talent as disposable resource vs. talent as cultivated steward; extractive hiring vs. generative growth; individual advancement vs. collective capability
summary: Develop talent as a living ecosystem where people grow through meaningful work tied to shared purpose, and the organization actively stewards their development as a benefit for everyone.

title: Growing Your Team's Skills Together
tension: Competency decay (skills erode without cultivation) vs. cultivation burden (continuous assessment and training costs attention and resources)
summary: Treat your workforce's knowledge as something you actively grow and refresh. Map what people know, spot gaps, and build skills that keep your business strong.

title: Guaranteeing Water for Everyone
tension: Algorithmic efficiency (automated rationing, disconnection, pricing) vs. human dignity (right to water, protection from shutoff, equitable access regardless of payment capacity)
summary: Ensure every household gets enough water to survive and thrive, funded by charging heavy users more while protecting those who can't afford it. Communities decide how the system works.

title: Guide Nature's Healing Timeline
tension: Intervention speed vs. Self-organizing resilience
summary: Work with how ecosystems naturally recover and change over time. Learn to recognize the stages, gently speed things up when needed, and let the system find its own balance rather than forcing a fixed end state.

title: Guiding Your Organization Through Change
tension: Speed of necessary change vs. continuity of identity and care for those affected
summary: Help your organization adapt and transform while keeping people grounded. Make change visible, build trust across divides, and care for those most affected.

title: Harvest Only What Grows Back
tension: Regeneration vs. Extraction: The rate at which a living system replenishes itself vs. the rate at which humans withdraw from it. Without explicit alignment, extraction exceeds regeneration and the resource base degrades irreversibly.
summary: Set sustainable extraction limits by measuring how fast ecosystems regenerate, then adjust those limits as conditions change. Science and communities decide together what's safe to take.

title: Harvest Only What Grows Back
tension: Regeneration vs. Extraction: The rate at which a living system replenishes itself vs. the rate at which humans withdraw from it. Without explicit alignment, extraction exceeds regeneration and the resource base degrades irreversibly.
summary: Set sustainable extraction limits by measuring how fast ecosystems regenerate, then adjust those limits as conditions change. Science and communities decide together what's safe to take.

title: Harvesting Forests That Heal Themselves
tension: Extraction vs. Regeneration — harvesting resources while preserving the forest's capacity to produce them
summary: Use clear rules and live forest data to remove trees thoughtfully, letting the forest regenerate stronger and more diverse while staying within what the ecosystem can handle.

title: Harvesting Wood Without Exhausting It
tension: Extraction vs. Regeneration — balancing immediate biomass yield against the time required for ecological recovery and the persistence of rooted carbon stocks.
summary: Time your cuts to match how fast trees regrow. This keeps forests productive, healthy, and carbon-rich for generations.

title: Heal Yourself, Raise Better Kids
tension: Reactive transmission of inherited patterns vs. conscious interruption and redesign of how we parent across generations
summary: Your own growth and healing directly shape your child's development. The work starts with you.

title: Healing Broken Pathways for Wildlife
tension: Structural connectivity (physical corridors exist) vs. Functional connectivity (species actually move and persist through them)
summary: Animals need to move across landscapes to survive. Find where habitat is broken up, then reconnect the pieces so populations can thrive.

title: Healing Broken Relationships
tension: Silent resentment that hardens into disconnection vs. authentic repair that strengthens bonds through vulnerability and accountability
summary: When harm happens, repair is a chance to build stronger trust. Structured practices for acknowledging hurt, taking responsibility, and restoring connection—showing that rupture can deepen relationships.

title: Healing Conflicts Through Community Care
tension: Punitive response vs. relational restoration
summary: Build systems where people resolve harm together through circles and mediation, empowering community members as skilled practitioners who transform conflict into accountability and healing.

title: Healing Land by Removing Invaders Wisely
tension: Eradication urgency vs. ecosystem resilience — removing threats fast enough to prevent permanent degradation, yet carefully enough that removal itself doesn't collapse the system.
summary: Remove invasive species in stages that match how nature heals itself, so native plants and animals can come back stronger. It's about timing and patience.

title: Healing Land, Resolving Borders
tension: Competing territorial authority vs. ecological continuity — how to resolve who belongs where without destroying the living system both depend on
summary: When groups fight over territory, restoring the damaged ecosystem together can resolve the conflict—turning shared repair work into the foundation for who gets recognized rights.

title: Healing Land Together
tension: Expert-driven restoration vs. community-rooted stewardship; short-term compliance vs. long-term ecosystem health; generic protocols vs. place-embedded practice
summary: Communities and ecologists work side by side to restore damaged landscapes, weaving in local knowledge and traditional practices while measuring what actually works.

title: Healing Peatlands by Restoring Water
tension: Rapid rewetting vs. ecosystem shock; local intervention vs. catchment-scale consequences; restoring historical hydrology vs. adapting to current land-use realities.
summary: Block old drainage ditches and manage water at landscape scale to let peatlands rebuild their natural water cycles and heal themselves.

title: Healing Poisoned Soil
tension: Toxicity accumulation vs. productive restoration — how to make degraded soils safe and fertile without merely displacing or isolating contamination.
summary: Find what's contaminating soil, then use plants and natural processes to clean it up. Monitor progress to make sure the land is safe for food and life again.

title: Healing Polluted Land Together
tension: Environmental remediation as displacement vs. remediation as commons stewardship
summary: Turn contaminated urban land into thriving commons by cleaning it up ecologically, governing it democratically, and creating real jobs—turning a toxic problem into community health, stable work, and living nature.

title: Healing Relationships After Trauma
tension: Safety through walls vs. safety through repair
summary: Rebuild trust and safety by practicing clear consent, quick repair when things go wrong, and tuning into how bodies respond. This transforms old protective patterns into genuine connection.

title: Healing Rivers from the Banks Up
tension: Immediate erosion control & invasive suppression vs. Long-term ecosystem resilience & self-sustaining regeneration
summary: Plant native vegetation along riverbanks to naturally prevent erosion, clean water, and support wildlife. The ecosystem rebuilds itself over time with minimal ongoing intervention.

title: Healing Salt-Damaged Land
tension: Salt accumulation (passive degradation) vs. salt stewardship (active flow management and restoration)
summary: Salt buildup poisons soil and water. Learn to measure it, flush it out, and grow plants that thrive in salty conditions to bring damaged ecosystems back to life.

title: Healing Soil After Disturbance
tension: Immediate productivity (requiring soil intervention) vs. Long-term soil aliveness (requiring minimal disturbance and recovery time)
summary: Learn to measure soil damage from tilling and guide it back to health by protecting the living networks underground that keep soil fertile for the long term.

title: Healing Soil by Changing What You Grow
tension: Short-term yield stability vs. long-term system regeneration; external input dependence vs. internal biological capacity
summary: Plant different crops in sequence to rebuild healthy soil, cut pest problems naturally, and free yourself from costly chemical inputs.

title: Healing Soil's Water Absorption
tension: Sealed soil (compaction, crusting, hydrophobicity) vs. Living soil (permeable, self-regulating, regenerative)
summary: Measure and restore how well soil soaks up and holds water by rebuilding its structure and life. This determines whether land floods or flourishes.

title: Healing Streams with Native Plants
tension: Fragmentation vs. Continuity — riparian zones lie severed by dams, roads, channelization, and conflict; restoration must weave them back into functioning corridors while respecting site-specific hydrology (ephemeral, montane, urban, dryland).
summary: Plant native vegetation along streams to filter pollution, slow water flow, and reconnect fragmented habitats. These living buffers adapt to local conditions and help watersheds function again.

title: Healing the Fungal Networks Under Our Feet
tension: Short-term management intervention vs. long-term network integrity and adaptive capacity
summary: Soil fungi connect everything underground. Learn to spot when these networks break down, help them recover, and manage land in ways that keep them thriving for the long term.

title: Healing the Living Soil Surface
tension: Protection vs. Intervention — knowing when to shield fragile crust communities from disturbance and when to break compacted surfaces to restore water flow
summary: Biocrusts are fragile living networks that make soil work. Learn to read their health, protect them from damage, and restore them where they're broken—bringing water and nutrients back to the land.

title: Healing Together, Not Alone
tension: Fragmented, episodic clinical access vs. integrated, continuous, community-woven mental health stewardship
summary: Build mental health support where people navigate care together, peers guide each other, and treatment feels continuous and whole—not fragmented appointments with strangers.

title: Healing Trauma at Your Own Pace
tension: Urgency to heal vs. the nervous system's need for graduated, paced exposure; isolation vs. relational safety; external protocols vs. somatic self-knowledge
summary: Match trauma processing to what your nervous system can handle right now. Too fast risks harm; too slow risks stuck. Find the right speed with skilled support.

title: Healing Trauma Through Your Body
tension: Frozen history (implicit trauma living in the body) vs. Present agency (capacity to distinguish now from then)
summary: Learn to calm your nervous system and tell the difference between old wounds and what's happening now. Process difficult memories safely by moving between calm and challenge, building resilience you can feel in your bones.

title: Healing Trust After Harm
tension: Hypervigilance (over-protection) vs. Openness (under-protection)
summary: Help people and teams recalibrate how they perceive safety and each other after trauma or conflict. Rebuild the foundation for belonging and mutual care.

title: Healing Watersheds After Fire
tension: Rapid stabilization vs. allowing ecosystem recovery; protecting downstream communities vs. respecting fire-adapted systems
summary: After fire strips the land bare, water runs wild and soil washes away. Smart intervention at the right moment can restore water cycles and protect everything downstream.

title: Healing When Your Values Get Broken
tension: Ethical integrity vs. systemic complicity — the gap between who you are and what you're required to do, and the path back to coherence.
summary: When systems force you to act against your beliefs, it wounds you deeply. This practice helps you name that pain, grieve it, and rebuild toward work that aligns with who you actually are.

title: Healthy Boundaries That Hold Families Together
tension: Autonomy of the couple/household unit vs. the pull and claims of extended family and inherited patterns
summary: Create clear agreements that let family members stay themselves while staying connected. Good boundaries protect both individual freedom and the relationships that matter most.

title: Healthy Soil Holds Together
tension: Soil structure (physical binding) vs. soil biology (living networks) — resolved when recognized as inseparable; aggregates are both the product and the proof of soil aliveness.
summary: Strong soil structure—where particles bind together—signals a living ecosystem. Measuring this tells you if your land is building carbon, supporting food webs, and recovering from damage.

title: Heat Your Way to Safe Compost
tension: Safety (pathogen elimination) vs. Aliveness (preserving decomposer communities and nutrient cycling)
summary: Use the natural heat of decomposition to kill pathogens in compost. Monitor temperature and feedstock to know when your pile is actually safe.

title: Help People Navigate by Feel
tension: Abstract signage & algorithmic navigation vs. embodied, sensory, narrative wayfinding rooted in lived place-knowledge
summary: Design places that work with how people actually find their way—using landmarks, sounds, textures, and memory—so everyone can navigate with confidence, not just those who read maps.

title: Helping Displaced Families Reclaim Their Land
tension: Historical dispossession vs. present occupation | Individual property rights vs. community reparative justice | Market valuation vs. genealogical claim
summary: Legal pathways for families displaced by redlining or forced removal to regain housing and control over their neighborhoods through documented ancestry—without needing to buy it outright. Funded through reparations.

title: Hidden Costs: Care Work in Budget Decisions
tension: Visibility bias (capital projects, individual benefit, tangible output) vs. Stewardship work (care, prevention, maintenance, collective thriving)
summary: Participatory budgeting often overlooks care work and shared community assets, leaving women and caregivers out of spending decisions that affect them most.

title: Hiring as a Living System
tension: Speed and throughput vs. carrying capacity and regeneration
summary: Stop treating hiring like a factory. Make visible what your team can actually sustain, set honest limits, and let feedback shape how you improve—so growth doesn't break the people you have.

title: Hold Money Until Work Is Really Done
tension: Trust vs. Verification — how to close a project equitably when asymmetric information and power create incentive to abandon or dispute work.
summary: Keep final payments in escrow while you verify all work meets standards, disputes are settled, and everyone's obligations are met. Release funds only when you're confident the project is actually complete.

title: Holding Multiple Truths at Once
tension: Coherence vs. Complexity — the pull toward settled single-lens certainty versus the necessity of holding contradictory frames to navigate adequately in complex systems.
summary: Learn to think from different worldviews without forcing them to agree. This builds wisdom, surfaces blind spots, and helps groups make better decisions together.

title: Holding Multiple Worlds at Once
tension: Fragmentation (compartmentalized, conflicted identities) vs. Assimilation (erasure of origin in service to belonging)
summary: How people across borders weave together their ancestral roots, languages, and homes into an integrated identity without choosing one over the other.

title: Holding Space for Inner Transformation
tension: Individual psychological safety vs. collective meaning-making; Pathologizing altered states vs. honoring their wisdom; Rapid insight vs. sustainable embodiment
summary: Communities that prepare people for consciousness work, support them through difficult moments, and help them make sense of what they learn. Treats these experiences as shared passages, not private crises.

title: Honoring Commitments You Actually Make
tension: Autonomy vs. Accountability — the need to choose freely AND to honour what you've chosen
summary: Treat your commitments as sacred promises, not casual contracts. Know what you're signing up for, check in regularly, and end things honestly when the time comes.

title: Honoring Competing Values Without Betraying Anyone
tension: Fidelity to competing legitimate values vs. the pressure to choose one and deny the other
summary: When your organization serves multiple legitimate goods that pull in different directions, map what's at stake, acknowledge the real trade-offs, and choose deliberately rather than pretending everyone wins.

title: Honoring Future Employee Security
tension: Securing binding commitments to future stakeholders vs. preserving capital for present growth and adaptation
summary: Treat pension promises as real obligations to real people, not just numbers on a balance sheet. Design fair funding so today's business stays healthy while tomorrow's retirees get what they're owed.

title: Honoring Indigenous Land Stewardship
tension: Colonial land dispossession & state-centric governance vs. indigenous territorial sovereignty & customary stewardship authority
summary: Recognize indigenous peoples as the primary decision-makers for their ancestral lands by integrating their customary laws, governance, and ecological knowledge into formal legal systems.

title: Houses Where Generations Help Each Other
tension: Care as isolated household burden vs. care as embedded social infrastructure
summary: Design neighborhoods where young people, families, and elders live close together and share caring responsibilities. Instead of market rent or age-segregated care homes, people earn housing security by supporting each other across generations.

title: Housing as Health Foundation
tension: Housing treated as commodity vs. housing stewarded as health commons; health systems absorbing housing-induced costs vs. preventing them upstream; fragmented care silos vs. integrated care anchored in place.
summary: When people have stable homes and cooperative control, preventive care thrives and health inequities shrink. Housing becomes the anchor that holds everything else together.

title: Housing for Living, Not Profit
tension: Exchange-Value Extraction vs. Use-Value Stewardship
summary: Stop treating homes as investment vehicles. Keep housing affordable and stable by shifting from extraction (landlords, speculation) to stewardship (residents, communities, public ownership).

title: Housing That Moves With People
tension: Permanent Settlement Assumption vs. Cyclical Labour Reality
summary: Design flexible homes for migrant and seasonal workers that welcome temporary stays, strengthen community ties, and turn seasonal movement into housing stability rather than instability.

title: Housing That Stays in Your Family
tension: Property Rights (landlord's absolute control over asset and occupants) vs. Habitation Rights (tenant's binding claim to remain, rooted in community membership and contribution)
summary: Legal protections that let tenants build real security and pass homes to their children, keeping families and neighborhoods stable without requiring ownership.

title: Housing Without Strings Attached
tension: Housing as right vs. housing as control mechanism — systems that treat shelter as entitlement requiring no surveillance or deservingness proof vs. systems that weaponize housing precarity to enforce compliance, criminalize survival, and enable deportation.
summary: Shelter as a right, not a reward or punishment. Separating housing access from criminal records, immigration status, and surveillance to make it truly available to everyone.

title: How Cities Let People Actually Decide
tension: Concentrated constitutional authority vs. distributed constituent power — the question of who shapes the rules that bind everyone.
summary: Communities design governance systems where citizen votes on major decisions are binding, not advisory. Power shifts hands through deliberate processes that make participation real.

title: How Commons Stay Fair and Free
tension: Distributed agency & autonomy vs. Collective accountability & resource preservation
summary: A framework where communities create clear rules, share real power, and adapt together to prevent anyone from taking over while keeping resources healthy for everyone.

title: How Communities Mark What Matters
tension: Atomization & forgetting vs. continuity & belonging — the constant pressure toward fragmentation that ritual counteracts through embodied, collective repetition.
summary: Rituals and ceremonies are how groups encode meaning, mark important transitions, pass knowledge forward, and stay connected through intentional, repeatable practice.

title: How Cooperatives Govern Themselves
tension: Individual benefit vs. collective resilience / Democratic voice vs. operational coherence / Growth ambition vs. member-centered purpose
summary: Members own and control the business together, sharing profits fairly and making decisions democratically. It's how people align their own interests with the group's success.

title: How Extended Families Share Housing and Care
tension: Individual housing security + life-stage flexibility vs. collective kinship obligation + compound stability
summary: Multigenerational compounds pool resources for housing, work, and welfare, adapting as people marry, age, and face hardship. Everyone has a say based on their life stage.

title: How First Stories Shape What's Possible
tension: Frame Stickiness vs. Deliberative Openness
summary: The way a group first frames a problem tends to stick around—and can block better solutions from even being considered. Reframing early and often keeps possibilities open.

title: How to Read for Real Growth
tension: Consumption velocity vs. comprehension depth; solitary extraction vs. collective meaning-making; breadth of exposure vs. mastery of foundations
summary: Turn reading into a living habit that deepens your thinking, expands how you see the world, and builds knowledge over time.

title: How to Talk Through Conflict
tension: Spontaneous reactivity vs. thoughtful stewardship of relational capacity
summary: Turn difficult conversations into healing moments. Structure, prepare, and practice speaking truthfully while staying connected to what others actually need.

title: How Your Posture Shapes How You Feel
tension: Postural habit (armor, collapse, compensation) vs. postural agency (felt aliveness, choice, adaptation)
summary: Learn to notice, release, and rebuild how you move and sit. Better alignment means better focus, less pain, and more energy for what matters.

title: Hunting That Doesn't Deplete Wildlife
tension: Human subsistence need vs. Wildlife population persistence
summary: Communities manage hunting as a shared resource by tying harvests to animal populations, rotating where people hunt, and blending ecological science with traditional knowledge to keep both wildlife and hunting alive.

title: Imagining Better Futures Together
tension: Imagination as escape vs. imagination as rigorous design; inner symbolic work vs. outer systemic change; individual vision vs. collective stewarding
summary: Use guided imagination practices to help people envision regenerative futures and connect personal dreams with collective wellbeing.

title: Indigenous Communities Controlling Their Own Economy
tension: External control & resource extraction vs. community sovereignty & regenerative circulation
summary: Indigenous peoples govern their own enterprises, manage their resources, and keep wealth circulating within their communities. It's about rejecting extraction and reclaiming control over their economic future.

title: Indigenous People Governing City Land
tension: Colonial cadastral grid (ownership, fragmentation, commodification) vs. Indigenous territorial stewardship (relationality, commons, cosmological alignment)
summary: How cities can recognize Indigenous peoples' ancestral connection to urban land and give them real power in decisions about that land, water, and cultural spaces.

title: Investing Money That Matches Your Values
tension: Wealth accumulation vs. Values fidelity | Financial return expectations vs. Justice outcomes | Capital availability vs. Mission alignment
summary: Choose where your capital goes by clarifying what you believe in, screening investments for alignment, and building a portfolio where making money and making impact work together, not against each other.

title: Jobs Come to Where People Live
tension: Radial transit networks optimized for CBD inflow vs. polycentric employment requiring suburb-to-suburb and periphery-to-employment mobility; employer self-interest in stable workforce vs. public transit funding gaps in low-income areas
summary: Require major employers to fund transit service bringing workers from surrounding neighborhoods, creating permanent routes that let people stay home while accessing opportunity.

title: Jobs for Local Workers First
tension: Wage labor as commodity (exploitative, extractive, mobile) vs. Work as membership in place-based stewardship (rooted, dignified, regenerative)
summary: Guarantee employment opportunities for city residents and vulnerable populations through local hiring requirements and investment in maintenance and service sector work.

title: Keep Cash Moving Through Your Business
tension: Growth & Stability vs. Cash Starvation & Idle Capital
summary: Master the rhythm of money flowing in and out so you spot problems early and keep your organization running smoothly.

title: Keep Communication Flowing and Alive
tension: Coherence vs. Responsiveness: How to maintain integrity of shared meaning while adapting to the learning pace, context, and readiness of diverse participants without collapsing into either monolithic broadcasting or fragmented chaos.
summary: Build communication like a living system: stay consistent without being rigid, keep channels healthy, match your message to who's ready to hear it, and make sure nothing breaks if one path fails.

title: Keep Design Sharp and Growing
tension: Theory vs. Practice — the gap between what works in abstraction and what survives contact with complexity and time.
summary: Use proven methods to design better, learn from what actually happens, and build your team's ability to improve over time.

title: Keep Equipment Running Before It Breaks
tension: Predictability vs. Decay | Planned stewardship vs. crisis response
summary: Stop waiting for machines to fail. Track their health, service them on schedule, and spot problems early so your business keeps moving.

title: Keep Forests Healthy and Fire-Safe
tension: Fire risk & carbon storage vs. biomass extraction & livelihood; Short-term safety vs. Long-term forest resilience
summary: Manage dead wood and plant buildup so forests can regenerate naturally, reduce wildfire risk, and use the harvested material wisely instead of letting it burn or go to waste.

title: Keep Good Customers Coming Back
tension: Early sensing of decline vs. adaptive intervention that preserves relationship health and reciprocal value
summary: Spot customers who might leave before they do, then reach out with the right offer at the right time. It's about staying connected, not scrambling to save relationships after they've broken down.

title: Keep Moving Through Life
tension: Specialization & Efficiency vs. Diversity & Adaptation
summary: Stay strong and independent by regularly assessing how your body moves, practicing varied exercises, and preventing falls before they happen.

title: Keep Procedures Honest and Alive
tension: Codified procedure vs. adaptive reality: Documentation hardens into brittle dogma, or procedures dissolve into invisible individual practice.
summary: Regularly walk through your documented processes with the people doing the work, catch where reality diverges from the handbook, and update accordingly. It keeps procedures useful instead of just existing.

title: Keep Promises You Can Measure
tension: Binding commitment vs. adaptive emergence — how to make promises durable without calcifying into brittle contracts
summary: Build trust by making clear commitments and automatically checking you're keeping them. When things drift, the system adapts without waiting for someone to notice.

title: Keep Technology in Step with Your Purpose
tension: Strategic intent vs. technological capability — the gap between what the organization needs to become and what its systems can enable.
summary: Build flexible technology plans that stay aligned with what your organization actually needs, evolving as both your strategy and capabilities grow.

title: Keep What You Learn When People Leave
tension: Knowledge as individual possession vs. knowledge as collective stewardship
summary: Capture and pass on what your organization knows before people walk out the door. Build rhythms of mentoring, documenting, and ritual that preserve hard-won expertise and help newcomers step up.

title: Keep Your Core Data Clean and Consistent
tension: Data entropy (drift, duplication, divergence across systems) vs. single source of truth (coherence, trustworthiness, actionability)
summary: Master data needs constant care, not just one-time fixes. Learn how to verify, deduplicate, and synchronize information across all your systems so everyone works with the same trusted facts.

title: Keep Your Data Reliable and Fresh
tension: Data as living flow vs. data as static artifact; predictability vs. responsiveness; centralized control vs. distributed stewardship
summary: Set up smart alerts when things go wrong, schedule regular updates to stay current, and define clear service standards so everyone knows what to expect.

title: Keep Your Data, Switch Your Service
tension: Data utility (shared access, integration, value) vs. data autonomy (sovereignty, portability, exit rights)
summary: Own your data and move it freely between platforms. Standards and open formats prevent companies from trapping you in their system.

title: Keep Your Options Open
tension: Committed execution (which builds momentum and focus) vs. preserved flexibility (which maintains adaptive capacity and resilience)
summary: Design decisions that let you wait, adapt, and change course as things become clearer instead of locking in too early.

title: Keep Your Product Line Sane
tension: Generative diversity (meeting actual market need) vs. entropic complexity (variants that consume capacity without proportional value)
summary: Too many product variants drain your team and confuse your customers. Set limits on what you'll offer, audit regularly to cut the waste, and focus on what actually sells.

title: Keep Your Product Portfolio Healthy
tension: Portfolio coherence (strategic alignment, resource focus) vs. Portfolio resilience (diversity, optionality, adaptation to shifting conditions)
summary: Know what you're offering, measure how it's performing, and retire things that no longer fit. A living portfolio that grows with your purpose, not against it.

title: Keep Your Skills Fresh Before They Fade
tension: Expertise as asset vs. expertise as liability — clinging to mastery that anchors you in a shrinking future vs. releasing it to make space for renewal
summary: Spot which capabilities are losing value, refresh them before they become useless, and build new ones faster than the world changes. Treat your skills like a garden that needs constant tending.

title: Keep Your Why, Change Your How
tension: Conviction vs. Rigidity — the risk that vision becomes either a compass (alive, adaptive) or a cage (brittle, identity-fused)
summary: Know what you're aiming for, but stay ready to change course. Check in with your purpose regularly and shift tactics without losing sight of what matters most.

title: Keeping a Record of Who Did What
tension: Accountability (need for transparent record of actions) vs. Burden (cost and complexity of retention, aggregation, and compliance)
summary: Create an unchangeable record of important actions in your system so you can prove what happened, when, and why—essential for accountability, troubleshooting, and compliance.

title: Keeping Alumni Connected and Growing
tension: Institutional knowledge loss vs. relational continuity; individual advancement vs. collective wisdom transmission
summary: Turn people who leave into lasting relationships. Pair them with current members for mentoring, career help, and financial support that benefits everyone.

title: Keeping Benefits Fair and Flowing
tension: Certainty vs. Adaptation — The need for fixed deadlines, clear rules, and auditable records versus the reality that eligibility, life circumstances, coverage adequacy, and community needs continuously evolve.
summary: Manage who gets covered, when they enroll, and how claims get paid—as a cycle of trust where everyone contributes and everyone's cared for.

title: Keeping Cash Moving at the Right Time
tension: Cash timing misalignment (obligations due before revenue arrives) vs. operational continuity (needing capital when it's needed, not when it's convenient)
summary: Match when money flows out with when it flows back in. Good timing keeps operations alive; bad timing kills them.

title: Keeping Cities Alive Together
tension: Individual freedom & private benefit vs. collective wellbeing & intergenerational flourishing
summary: How neighborhoods, parks, and local food systems thrive when communities share stewardship across generations—and how to measure what actually matters beyond money.

title: Keeping Cities Fair When Crisis Hits
tension: Speed vs. Legitimacy — crises demand rapid decisions that bypass deliberation, yet suspended accountability erodes the trust required for post-crisis recovery and invites permanent authority capture.
summary: Design emergency systems that make decisions transparently, allocate resources fairly to all neighborhoods, and automatically reset once the crisis ends. Legitimacy and equity shouldn't pause when emergencies start.

title: Keeping Communities Rooted
tension: Market-driven change velocity vs. community adaptation capacity; invisible displacement externalities vs. visible governance thresholds
summary: Stop displacement before it happens by making its impact visible, giving communities real say over neighborhood change, and pairing new development with protections that keep people in their homes.

title: Keeping Competition from Squashing Diversity
tension: Preserving species diversity vs. allowing dominant competitors to shape community structure naturally
summary: Watch for species being squeezed out by stronger competitors, then step in with the right moves to keep ecosystems diverse as they change naturally.

title: Keeping Contracts Alive and Fair
tension: Contractual compliance (rigid, adversarial, legalistic) vs. relational stewardship (adaptive, cooperative, trust-based)
summary: Manage contracts as agreements that grow and change with your relationships. Track who owes what, handle changes thoughtfully, and keep trust intact when conditions shift.

title: Keeping Craft Skills Alive Together
tension: Preservation vs. Vitality — keeping heritage craft alive as living practice embedded in economy and community, rather than as nostalgic museum artifact or lost knowledge.
summary: Formalize how experienced craftspeople pass skills to apprentices through structured programs and community recognition, ensuring heritage crafts survive in living practice rather than museums.

title: Keeping Crafts Alive in Neighborhoods
tension: Economic homogenization & monoculture vs. occupational distinctiveness & craft genealogy
summary: Map and strengthen the trades, skills, and family businesses that define a neighborhood's character and economic backbone across generations.

title: Keeping Crop Genes Alive
tension: Genetic erosion (loss of alleles, diversity, trait complexity) vs. adaptive resilience (the living library of variation that allows crops to evolve with climate, pests, and local conditions)
summary: Track and protect the genetic diversity of crops and their wild cousins so farmers can adapt to change and future generations inherit resilient plants.

title: Keeping Culture Alive as You Grow
tension: Culture as declared vs. culture as lived; monolithic coherence vs. adaptive pluralism
summary: Culture thrives through steady attention, not annual checkups. Create rhythms of reflection and response that help your values survive growth, change, and the people who join you.

title: Keeping Culture Alive Together
tension: Museum preservation (frozen, expert-controlled, wealth-extractive) vs. Living stewardship (adaptive, community-governed, value-circulating)
summary: How communities can own and maintain their cultural heritage through shared governance, stable funding, and adaptive reuse—rather than leaving it to experts or letting it decay.

title: Keeping Customers Coming Back
tension: Extractive transaction logic (maximize immediate value) vs. Regenerative stewardship logic (cultivate mutual flourishing)
summary: Build lasting relationships by understanding what keeps customers happy, celebrating their wins, and staying genuinely useful over time—not just at checkout.

title: Keeping Dangerous Materials Safe
tension: Containment vs. Flow — how to move necessary but dangerous materials safely while preventing cascading contamination and maintaining real-time visibility.
summary: Track hazardous materials from storage to disposal with transparency and care. Turn compliance into a system that actually protects people and the environment.

title: Keeping Data Clean and Traceable
tension: Data as ephemeral asset (move fast, extract value) vs. Data as living record (trace origin, verify integrity, retire safely)
summary: Track where your data comes from, how it changes, and where it goes. Make sure it stays accurate and safe every step of the way.

title: Keeping Data Safe and Usable
tension: Knowing what data you hold and its risks vs. the continuous drift of data as systems evolve, contexts change, and sensitivity classifications degrade over time.
summary: A way to figure out what data needs protecting, who can use it, and how to keep it secure—while still letting people do their work. It's something you maintain and adjust as things change.

title: Keeping Data Trustworthy Over Time
tension: Data quality as static compliance checkpoint vs. data quality as living, continuously-monitored ecosystem requiring adaptive stewardship
summary: Set up continuous checks that spot when data gets stale or unreliable, then fix problems before they cause real damage. Think of it like health monitoring for your data.

title: Keeping Design Honest Over Time
tension: Speed to market vs. Fidelity to circularity intent; Distributed autonomy vs. Coherent specification
summary: Set up regular checkpoints and clear rules for how products change, so they stay durable, repairable, and made responsibly from start to finish.

title: Keeping Development Benefits in the Community
tension: Developer capture of unearned value increment vs. Community stewardship of shared land value
summary: When developers build, residents get a say in what stays behind. Binding agreements, escrow funds, and shared governance ensure community wealth doesn't disappear—it stays rooted.

title: Keeping Distributed Teams on the Same Page
tension: Autonomy vs. Coherence — distributed decision-making that serves the whole without collapsing into either fragmentation or recentralization
summary: How autonomous business units stay aligned without losing their independence. Uses shared charters, regular check-ins, and mutual accountability to balance freedom with coherence.

title: Keeping Employee Records Honest
tension: Centralized authority vs. distributed stewardship — between a single system of record (brittle, hard to keep current) and decentralized ownership (fragmented, conflicting)
summary: Make sure employee data stays accurate and fair across your organization. When records are scattered, outdated, or wrong, people suffer—and so does trust.

title: Keeping Encryption Strong Over Time
tension: Static security mandates vs. adaptive cryptographic stewardship
summary: Manage encryption like any other system that ages and needs updating. Choose the right algorithms, rotate keys regularly, and retire old ones before they become weak—staying ahead of threats while keeping everything auditable.

title: Keeping Energy Affordable and Available
tension: Individual energy security (autonomous systems, debt avoidance, efficiency gains) vs. collective energy resilience (grid stability, universal access, burden-sharing across generations)
summary: How communities can ensure everyone has reliable, affordable energy by governing it together, protecting people from price shocks, and building systems that actually last.

title: Keeping Everything Intact During Ownership Changes
tension: Continuity vs. Control — the acquiring party needs assurance of asset and relationship integrity, while the departing party must protect its legacy and reputation during handoff.
summary: When a business changes hands, protect relationships, data, and commitments so nothing falls through the cracks and everyone stays on solid ground.

title: Keeping Family Businesses Strong Across Generations
tension: Emotional bonds that create resilience vs. role confusion that creates paralysis; multi-generational commitment vs. decision-making velocity; family loyalty vs. meritocratic capability
summary: How family-owned businesses stay healthy through clear decision-making, planned leadership transitions, and structures that resolve disagreements before they damage relationships or the company.

title: Keeping Farm Animals Resilient
tension: Genetic uniformity & market consolidation vs. adaptive diversity & place-based resilience
summary: Communities breed livestock together for local conditions, preserving rare breeds and genetic diversity as shared resources that adapt to changing landscapes and survive across generations.

title: Keeping Fisheries Alive Through Monitoring
tension: Extractive pressure vs. regenerative capacity — knowing the line between sustainable yield and system collapse
summary: Watch fish populations, habitats, and catches closely enough to adjust fishing before damage happens. It's about harvesting sustainably by staying ahead of problems.

title: Keeping Food in Circulation
tension: Artificial disposal vs. living recirculation: supply chains engineered for convenience create surplus that vanishes into waste, even as need persists; recapturing it requires breaking isolation between actors and redistributing governance itself.
summary: Food businesses, institutions, and communities work together to rescue surplus food and turn it into nourishment. Everyone stays accountable for preventing waste before it happens.

title: Keeping Founder Wisdom Alive
tension: Founder as irreplaceable bottleneck vs. Founder as cultivated resource whose wisdom outlives their role
summary: When founders leave, their hard-won knowledge shouldn't walk out the door. Learn how to capture what they know, plan smooth transitions, and build their values into how your organization works.

title: Keeping Genes Healthy While Harvesting
tension: Immediate harvest yield vs. long-term adaptive capacity of populations
summary: Balance what you take from nature with what you need to preserve—keeping diverse genes flowing between wild, farmed, and restored populations so they stay adaptable.

title: Keeping Goods Moving Through the Dock
tension: Throughput velocity (goods must move faster) vs. Capacity constraint (dock doors, staging space, sorting bandwidth are fixed)
summary: Coordinate when trucks arrive, park, and leave to prevent bottlenecks. Use real-time visibility and alerts to match each shipment to the right dock at the right time.

title: Keeping Hope Alive in Hard Work
tension: Sustaining agency and meaning over time vs. the corrosive weight of setback, exhaustion, and mortality awareness
summary: How to sustain hope as a real practice—grounded in what's actually happening, built with others, and refreshed by small wins—so you can keep going even when outcomes are uncertain.

title: Keeping Housing Affordable Forever
tension: Permanence vs. Erosion — the systemic pressure to convert community-serving assets into speculative commodities through exit clauses, waivers, sunset provisions, and refinancing loopholes.
summary: Use legal covenants to lock in affordable housing permanently, preventing speculation while managing long-term enforcement and exit options.

title: Keeping Housing in the Family
tension: Individual market ownership (forced sale, displacement, speculation) vs. Familial stewardship (multi-generational occupancy, affordability persistence, accumulated equity retained within family lines)
summary: A way for families to pass down affordable homes across generations through legal protections that lock in affordability and prevent speculation from pushing them out.

title: Keeping Inventory Fresh and Honest
tension: Accumulation vs. Flow — the tendency of inventory systems to calcify into dead stock versus the living circulation that serves actual need.
summary: Regular checks and smart aging practices prevent dead stock from piling up. Know what you actually have and what it's worth.

title: Keeping Investors Honest and Grounded
tension: Promise vs. Delivery — the gap between what investors expect and what the organization can actually sustain.
summary: Build real trust with investors by communicating clearly and regularly about what's actually happening—not what sounds good. Mismatched expectations destroy relationships; aligned ones last.

title: Keeping Investors in the Loop
tension: Transparency vs. Strategic Protection | Accountability vs. Autonomy
summary: Create honest, two-way conversations between owners and leaders so trust stays strong and money keeps flowing toward long-term growth.

title: Keeping Knowledge Alive Across Time
tension: Individual expertise fades with departure vs. collective wisdom accumulates and guides
summary: Build systems to preserve what your organization knows—decisions, relationships, lessons—so wisdom survives leadership changes and new people can learn from what came before.

title: Keeping Knowledge Alive and Shared
tension: Knowledge as locked-in individual asset vs. knowledge as shared, evolving commonwealth
summary: Capture what your people know, decide who can use it, and make sure valuable ideas don't walk out the door. Done right, knowledge becomes an asset everyone can build on.

title: Keeping Knowledge Fresh and Findable
tension: Knowledge as static asset (decays silently) vs. knowledge as living practice (requires continuous cultivation)
summary: Knowledge gets stale and scattered over time. Stay on top of what matters by tracking decay, refreshing understanding in regular cycles, and keeping old versions organized so nothing important gets lost.

title: Keeping Knowledge From Walking Out the Door
tension: Brittle concentration (critical function locked in one person or vesting cliff) vs. Resilient distribution (capacity spread across time, people, and governance)
summary: Spread critical skills across your team and tie people to the mission so expertise doesn't vanish when someone leaves. Build systems that catch problems early.

title: Keeping Land Affordable Forever
tension: Individual property ownership & speculative extraction vs. Collective stewardship & intergenerational equity
summary: Community land trusts remove land from speculation by holding it in permanent trust, keeping housing affordable across generations while giving residents real control over their neighborhoods.

title: Keeping Land Healthy for the Next Generation
tension: Speculative markets vs. intergenerational ecological accountability; individual property rights vs. collective regenerative duty
summary: Communities buy and hold land together forever, legally binding it to ecological healing and keeping it out of developers' hands. The land stays protected no matter who lives there or when.

title: Keeping Land in Many Hands
tension: Consolidation (capital efficiency, developer control) vs. Fragmentation (stewardship distribution, incremental resilience)
summary: Zoning rules that prevent developers from buying up plots and consolidating them, while creating legal pathways for communities and cooperatives to assemble land together. It's about stopping land monopolies before they start.

title: Keeping Leaders Answerable to People
