summary: Track where carbon goes in ecosystems and human activities to see true costs, hold people accountable, and help communities govern their impact within planetary limits.

title: Making Care Central to How Cities Work
tension: Care work as invisible infrastructure vs. care work as explicit, compensated, governing force
summary: Recognize care work as essential infrastructure. Build it into decisions, budgets, and systems—paying workers fairly and centering the people who hold communities together.

title: Making Care Part of Getting Around
tension: Mobility as individual transportation vs. mobility as shared care infrastructure; treating care as private burden vs. recognizing care as essential public system
summary: Transit hubs that weave in childcare, health services, and elder care—designed with communities so people can handle life's responsibilities while moving through the city.

title: Making Care Work Visible and Accessible
tension: Participation as individual choice vs. participation as dependent on invisible care work; care as private responsibility vs. care as collective infrastructure
summary: Support care services and recognize care workers so more people can participate fully in community life. When childcare and dependent care are affordable and valued, everyone benefits.

title: Making Cities Calmer for Everyone
tension: Sensory abundance (for some) vs. sensory deprivation (for others); overstimulation vs. understimulation; designed sensory control vs. sensory autonomy
summary: Design neighborhoods that work for all nervous systems—with quiet refuges, sensory variety, and protection from overwhelming stimulation. It matters because cities aren't comfortable for everyone right now.

title: Making Cities Pay for Algorithm Mistakes
tension: Algorithmic systems concentrate benefit capture while dispersing harm across residents who bear injury costs invisibly vs. making harm visible, financially traceable, and collectively stewarded through reserve funds and performance verification.
summary: Cities create funds that hold tech vendors financially responsible when their algorithms cause harm, making problems visible and giving residents real recourse when things go wrong.

title: Making Compliance Everyone's Job
tension: Compliance as rigid constraint vs. Compliance as adaptive stewardship
summary: Build systems where compliance isn't a final checkpoint but something teams see, understand, and own together throughout development—turning rules into shared responsibility.

title: Making Decisions Everyone Can See
tension: Transparency vs. Community Authority — how to make governance visible enough to prevent capture and enable accountability, without surrendering decision-making authority to external scrutiny or creating paralysis through over-documentation.
summary: Build systems where governance choices, ecological data, and resource flows stay visible and open to community scrutiny. This keeps power distributed and lets you adapt as conditions change.

title: Making Decisions for Tomorrow, Not Just Today
tension: Immediate visible needs vs. long-term intergenerational flourishing; present participants' preferences vs. absent future generations' interests; productivity time vs. relational & ecological time
summary: How to build governance that balances what we need now with what future generations will inherit, breaking the cycle of short-term thinking that locks in unfair outcomes.

title: Making Decisions Today for Tomorrow's Generation
tension: Present generation's need for resource benefit vs. future generation's right to inherit uncompromised capacity; short-term expedience vs. long-term fiduciary duty.
summary: Legal agreements that bind us to care for shared resources forever, with a voice in decisions for the people who'll inherit them.

title: Making Decisions Together Across Teams
tension: Autonomy vs. Coherence: How can distributed decision-making preserve organizational alignment without centralizing power or creating gridlock?
summary: How to spread decision-making power across your organization so each team owns their domain, stays accountable, and stays connected through honest feedback and mutual agreement.

title: Making Delivery Networks That Adapt
tension: Centralized cost extraction vs. distributed adaptive resilience
summary: Build fulfillment systems that stay flexible and resilient by spreading decisions across local teams, not optimizing for speed alone. Redundancy and local control matter more than pure efficiency.

title: Making Elderhood Matter
tension: Cultural erasure of aging vitality vs. personal agency in constructing elderhood as a generative life stage
summary: Reimagining aging as a time of wisdom and contribution, not decline. Building communities where older people stay independent, connected, and valued across generations.

title: Making Empty Buildings Expensive
tension: Speculation & extraction (land as financial asset) vs. Occupancy & stewardship (land as inhabited commons)
summary: Tax vacant or speculative properties so heavily that sitting on land stops making financial sense. Forces owners to develop, occupy, or sell—while the revenue funds community land purchases and neighbourhood stability.

title: Making Friends With Your Body
tension: Body-as-mirror (external evaluation, shame, disconnection) vs. Body-as-instrument (functional capability, sensory aliveness, somatic belonging)
summary: Move from judging how you look to noticing how your body feels and what it can do. Simple sensory practices help you experience your body as home, not an object to criticize.

title: Making Gratitude a Daily Habit
tension: Habituation & taking-for-granted vs. Active attention & generative acknowledgment
summary: Build regular practices of specific appreciation that shift how you see abundance and strengthen bonds with others over time.

title: Making Growth Fair for Everyone
tension: Extractive attention capture vs. reciprocal attention stewardship
summary: Design systems where growth benefits spread across users, creators, and platforms—making it clear who gains from attention and ensuring everyone shares the rewards.

title: Making Hidden Health Hazards Visible
tension: Invisible environmental degradation vs. deliberate environmental stewardship
summary: Identify and reduce the invisible environmental stressors—toxins, poor air, noise—that wear down health. Design spaces that help people recover, not just survive.

title: Making Invisible Relationship Agreements Visible
tension: Unspoken assumptions that erode trust vs. explicit negotiation that deepens mutuality
summary: Surface the hidden expectations, needs, and patterns in your relationships so they can grow and adapt instead of breaking down under unstated pressure.

title: Making It Safe to Speak Up
tension: Silence (driven by fear of retaliation) vs. Visibility (driven by need for systemic healing and accountability)
summary: How organizations create trusted channels for people to report problems—and actually protect them when they do. It's how companies catch serious issues before they become crises.

title: Making It Safe to Tell the Truth
tension: Individual safety vs. collective integrity
summary: A commons stays healthy when members can safely report problems without fear of retaliation. This means building systems and culture where speaking up about harm is normal stewardship, not a risky act of heroism.

title: Making Knowledge Travel
tension: Depth vs. Breadth — the specialist risks obsolescence; the generalist risks superficiality.
summary: Turn what you know into skills others can use. Build expertise that adapts, spreads, and lasts across different situations.

title: Making Land Care Everyone's Job
tension: Professional maintenance (knowledge erased, ecology degraded, care outsourced) vs. Resident stewardship (knowledge cultivated, ecology regenerated, care embedded in identity)
summary: Turn ecological restoration from hired work into shared responsibility. Residents become stewards through governance, leases, and seasonal labor, rebuilding land together as commons practice.

title: Making Language Work Matter
tension: Linguistic homogenization (dominant language as invisible default) vs. linguistic pluralism as active stewardship (translation as governance infrastructure and honored labor)
summary: Translation isn't an add-on—it's core stewardship. Pay for it, protect it, and watch how multilingual communities participate more fully in decisions that affect them.

title: Making Maintenance Matter in Budget Decisions
tension: Immediate tangible visibility vs. structural systems invisibility; present preferences vs. future liabilities
summary: How communities can stop ignoring upkeep work and make sure maintenance gets funded and valued the same way new projects do, so shared infrastructure actually lasts.

title: Making Mergers Work for Everyone
tension: Speed of capital consolidation vs. preservation of living systems and adaptive capacity
summary: How to bring two companies together without losing what made them valuable. Keep the best parts of each culture while building something stronger.

title: Making Metrics Trustworthy
tension: Comparability vs. Context | Standardization vs. Meaning
summary: Set up shared ownership and clear versioning for metrics so teams can learn together without losing context or gaming the numbers.

title: Making Money Choices That Matter
tension: Invisible trade-offs (what we don't see) vs. visible gains (what we pursue) — leading to drift, misalignment, and resource waste.
summary: Stop letting money decisions happen to you. See what you're really trading off, let go of what's already spent, and choose based on what actually matters to you.

title: Making Money Flows Visible
tension: Opacity (protecting operational discretion, competitive advantage, hierarchy) vs. Legibility (enabling participation, accountability, informed stewardship)
summary: Show everyone where money actually goes and what it costs—financially, ecologically, socially. Transparency enables fair decisions and continuous learning.

title: Making Money Movements Visible
tension: Opacity vs. Traceability — the need to record financial reality comprehensively while keeping that evidence accessible, queryable, and reproducible across time, entities, and stakeholder scrutiny.
summary: Build clear records of every financial transaction so anyone can trace money from start to finish and verify it's accurate. Trust grows from evidence, not just someone saying it's okay.

title: Making Nature's Costs Visible
tension: Hidden environmental externalities vs. Transparent ecological accountability
summary: Count the real damage your choices cause to nature, then redesign how you work to heal that damage and leave things better than you found them.

title: Making Neighbourhood Care Visible
tension: Care as invisible, dispersed, undervalued labour vs. Care as stewarded, visible, reciprocal commonwealth
summary: Map and coordinate the care work already happening in your neighbourhood—childcare, elder support, meal-sharing—so it's valued, supported, and easier for people to find and join.

title: Making Old Factories Community Assets
tension: Erasure vs. Reactivation — the choice between clearing industrial sites to erase painful labour histories, or stewarding them as living archives that honour workers while enabling contemporary production and community belonging.
summary: Turn abandoned industrial sites into places where people work, gather, and remember—keeping the buildings, their stories, and the skills they represent alive for everyone.

title: Making Peace With Your Inner Voices
tension: Fragmentation vs. Forced Integration — honoring protective multiplicity while restoring cooperative function
summary: Learn to recognize the different parts of yourself, honor what each one needs, and help them work together instead of against you. A path to internal harmony.

title: Making Performance Spaces Community Owned
tension: Extractive cultural ownership (venue as real estate, audience as consumers, artists as suppliers) vs. Stewardship model (venue as shared cultural infrastructure, audience as co-governors, artists as dignified contributors)
summary: When a city's concert halls and theaters are owned by the people who use them, artists get paid fairly and tickets stay affordable. Communities decide what gets performed and who benefits.

title: Making Pollinators Legal Citizens
tension: Individual land use rights vs. collective dependence on pollinator populations for food security and ecosystem function
summary: Give pollinators the same legal protections as other members of your ecosystem. Restrict harmful chemicals, designate safe habitat zones, and spread stewardship across all landholders so agriculture and neighborhoods become places where pollinators thrive.

title: Making Power Visible and Fair
tension: Invisible power (silent accumulation, structural dominance, unexamined privilege) vs. Stewarded power (named, audited, redistributed for justice)
summary: Power shapes every commons, and hidden power corrodes trust. Learn to name it, analyze it together, and redistribute it deliberately through transparent structures.

title: Making Power Visible Through Transparency
tension: Information asymmetry as tool of domination vs. information flows as foundation of just governance
summary: When some people know more than others, trust breaks down. Design systems that share information openly so everyone can see how decisions get made and who holds power.

title: Making Promises to the Land
tension: Extraction vs. Regeneration — the choice between taking what the system can bear and actively restoring what has been taken.
summary: A framework where humans and ecosystems pledge mutual care through ceremony and practice. Communities commit to regenerating what they take, monitored and renewed seasonally.

title: Making Purpose Work in Daily Decisions
tension: Purpose as static identity vs. purpose as living, evolving governance mechanism
summary: Purpose isn't inspiration—it's operational logic. When built into how organizations actually work, it guides what they do, settles conflicts, and gets renewed regularly to stay alive.

title: Making Rules Work for Everyone
tension: Regulatory compliance as external burden vs. compliance as internalized stewardship; centralized gatekeeping vs. distributed competent authority
summary: Build a system where regulatory requirements stay visible and understandable, local teams handle decisions they're equipped to make, and staying compliant is something you do continuously, not just when inspectors show up.

title: Making Rules Work for You
tension: Compliance as external compliance cost vs. Compliance as adaptive governance signal
summary: Turn compliance from a burden into a source of strength. Build systems that adapt to changing rules while keeping everyone accountable.

title: Making Sense of Messy Problems
tension: Oversimplification (missing causal factors, creating cascading failures) vs. Overwhelming complexity (paralysis, implementation collapse, false certainty)
summary: Build the skills to understand and talk about genuinely complex challenges without pretending to have simple answers or getting paralyzed by uncertainty. Match your solutions to the real problem, not an oversimplified version of it.

title: Making Sense Together
tension: Individual interpretation (incomplete, isolated) vs. Collective sense-making (risk of groupthink) — resolved through structured dialogue that preserves dissent while building coherent shared frameworks.
summary: Help groups think through complex problems together by surfacing different viewpoints, building real agreement, and avoiding both forced consensus and decision paralysis.

title: Making Service Promises You Can Keep
tension: Accountability vs. Autonomy — how to bind service providers to commitments without ossifying the system or displacing responsibility onto metrics.
summary: Set clear service standards, measure them honestly, and follow through. When both sides know what to expect and hold each other accountable, trust actually works.

title: Making Shrinking Towns Worth Staying In
tension: Accept demographic collapse vs. engineer artificial growth | RESOLVES TO: Steward natural flows while maintaining essential services and intergenerational viability
summary: Stop trying to reverse decline. Instead, keep the people who belong there, attract newcomers looking for alternatives, cluster services around who actually lives there now, and build shared spaces that make staying possible.

title: Making Soil Everyone's Responsibility
tension: Extractive use (depletion, compaction, contamination) vs. Regenerative stewardship (building living capacity, healing legacy damage, ensuring heritable fertility)
summary: A legal framework that treats soil as a living commons, sets measurable health standards, and holds people accountable for damage—requiring restoration across generations.

title: Making Spending Transparent and Fair
tension: Trust vs. Control — how to enable distributed spending while maintaining systemic integrity without collapsing into either blind permission or paralyzing surveillance.
summary: Set up clear rules for how money gets spent across your organization—so everyone knows what's allowed, decisions are shared, and spending stays honest without feeling like policing.

title: Making Street Markets Count
tension: Visibility & Legitimation vs. Erasure & Criminalization
summary: Street vendors and informal traders are essential infrastructure. They deserve visibility, legal protection, and space to thrive—not pressure to disappear or pretend to be something else.

title: Making Street Vending Fair and Secure
tension: Formalization that dignifies vs. formalization that dispossesses; protecting vendor livelihoods and territorial customs vs. managing shared public space fairly
summary: Street vendors need dignity, stability, and a real say in how public space gets used. Participatory governance creates frameworks that protect livelihoods while sharing space and revenue fairly.

title: Making Streets Come Alive
tension: Private property control vs. shared street vitality; speculative land holding vs. lived neighbourhood stewardship
summary: Lively streets need activity at ground level. Require mixed-use storefronts, open sightlines, and street-facing windows so people naturally watch the street and care for it.

title: Making Streets Safe in Informal Neighborhoods
tension: Dignity via participation vs. Dignity via formalization—respecting existing movement patterns and informal governance while securing tenure, infrastructure investment, and anti-displacement protection.
summary: Communities design and protect pathways and street economies together, ensuring everyone can walk safely and earn a living without fear of losing their home.

title: Making Supply Chain Emissions Visible
tension: Controlling what you cannot see vs. stewarding what you share responsibility for
summary: Track where carbon actually comes from in your supply chain, share responsibility fairly with suppliers, and build partnerships that regenerate—not just reduce.

title: Making Sure Carbon Claims Are Real
tension: Credible climate action vs. phantom carbon credits that obscure rather than solve atmospheric overload
summary: How to verify that carbon reduction projects actually work and don't just move the problem elsewhere. Separates genuine climate action from greenwashing.

title: Making Sure Carbon Stays Locked Away
tension: Accounting certainty vs. ecological reality: carbon claimed as 'permanent' may be released through disturbance, decomposition, or climate change, making permanence claims unreliable without continuous verification.
summary: Carbon offsets only work if the carbon actually stays out of the atmosphere. This pattern helps you monitor whether stored carbon will really last, even as climate and conditions change.

title: Making Sure Commons Work Pays
tension: Stewardship sustainability vs. commons affordability; invisible labor recognition vs. exploitation; livelihood security vs. free-riding prevention
summary: A commitment that everyone who keeps the commons running—especially caretakers—earns enough to live on and gets recognized for their work. No hidden labor. No poverty wages.

title: Making Sure Everyone Gets Fed
tension: Maximizing extraction from a value chain vs. sustaining the health and regeneration of all participants within it
summary: Map where value flows in your network, spot where it leaks or gets hoarded, then redesign so all contributors actually thrive.

title: Making Sure Rewards Match Your Goals
tension: Stated intent vs. actual incentive; individual motivation vs. collective thriving; short-term extraction vs. long-term stewardship
summary: Your incentive systems often reward the wrong behaviors. Audit what you actually encourage, then redesign to align personal motivation with collective and systemic health.

title: Making Systems Talk to Each Other
tension: System autonomy vs. coherent value flow
summary: Connect your specialized tools so they work together naturally and adapt when things change, rather than forcing rigid connections that break under pressure.

title: Making Teamwork Visible and Fair
tension: Concentration of expertise (bottleneck, fragility) vs. distributed capability (diffusion, coordination cost)
summary: Help teams solve problems together by showing who depends on whom, rewarding people for helping, and building trust through honest feedback.

title: Making Things Affordable for Everyone
tension: Universal access vs. financial sustainability | Entry-cost reduction vs. long-term revenue stability
summary: Design pricing and ownership models that serve people across income levels—renting instead of buying, sliding scale fees, or having wealthier customers help subsidize access for those with less.

title: Making Things Right Again
tension: One-time apology (performative closure) vs. sustained repair (living accountability)
summary: How people and communities rebuild trust through honest apology, meaningful repair, and the harder work of actually changing behavior over time.

title: Making Time for Everyone
tension: Standardized participation timings (that privilege the unencumbered) vs. honoring the lived temporality of caregivers, precarious workers, seasonal laborers, and those managing time poverty
summary: Design governance that works around people's real schedules—not everyone has free evenings. Honor care work, protect paid time, and share scheduling burdens fairly.

title: Making Trade Compliance Work for Everyone
tension: Opacity & Risk vs. Transparency & Collective Stewardship
summary: Turn customs and border operations into a shared system where compliance is transparent, traceable, and governed together. What usually costs businesses time and money becomes a trustworthy commons that strengthens the whole supply chain.

title: Making Water Everyone's Responsibility
tension: Hidden utility vs. visible commons | Individual consumption vs. collective stewardship | Privatised access vs. equitable right
summary: When people see how water moves through their city—where it comes from, where it goes, who controls it—they can actually govern it together. Visible water infrastructure becomes a tool for fairness, ecological healing, and belonging.

title: Making Work Fair for Everyone
tension: Capital's demand for flexibility vs. workers' need for security, voice, and dignified livelihood
summary: How organizations treat all workers—employees, contractors, gig workers—with fair pay, real voice, and dignity. When this works, workers thrive and businesses become more resilient.

title: Making Work Flow Visible and Steady
tension: Predictable flow vs. adaptive responsiveness
summary: Show how work moves through your operation, sync teams around shared rhythms, and protect capacity so you stay reliable without losing flexibility to change.

title: Making Workspace Work for Everyone
tension: Individual ergonomic need & comfort vs. collective space stewardship & fair access
summary: Design and manage shared physical spaces so they're comfortable, accessible, and used fairly—giving everyone a voice in how the workspace actually serves them.

title: Making Zoning Decisions Together
tension: Zoning as inherited, opaque, calcified power vs. zoning as continuously re-negotiated commons subject to democratic scrutiny and adaptive revision
summary: Give residents real say in how land-use rules get made and changed, so zoning stays accountable to current communities instead of locked into outdated decisions or hidden in algorithms.

title: Managing Accounts Across Your Organization
tension: Concentration of account knowledge in individual stewards vs. systemic resilience and shared governance across relationship transitions and financial cycles
summary: Set up clear cycles for planning, handoffs, and reconciliation so different levels of your business stay aligned on what's working and what needs attention.

title: Managing Carbon Through Watersheds
tension: Carbon escape (export, loss, atmospheric release) vs. carbon retention and cycling (sequestration, burial, biological productivity)
summary: Track how carbon moves through water systems and use that knowledge to restore natural carbon storage—turning watersheds into places that trap carbon instead of releasing it.

title: Managing Credit Without Breaking Trust
tension: Trust extended today vs. certainty of repayment tomorrow
summary: Set lending limits, watch for trouble early, and handle missed payments in ways that keep relationships intact. A framework for lending that stays resilient when people can't pay.

title: Managing Damage Claims in Logistics
tension: Fragmented damage assessment (local, reactive, siloed) vs. systemic visibility (unified observation, root cause understanding, collective accountability)
summary: Handle shipping damage systematically through proper assessment, documentation, and insurance verification to protect your business and recover losses.

title: Managing Data From Birth to Deletion
tension: Keeping data long enough to serve legitimate purposes (compliance, audit, operational need) vs. holding it so long that storage costs, privacy risks, and complexity spiral beyond benefit.
summary: Decide what data you keep, for how long, and when to delete it. A thoughtful approach protects you legally while respecting privacy and reducing clutter.

title: Managing Debt Before It Manages You
tension: Short-term expedience vs. long-term regeneration capacity
summary: Track financial and technical debts like living commitments. Make obligations visible, pay them down within what you can handle, and forgive strategically so debt doesn't trap your organization.

title: Managing Distributed Work Fairly
tension: Individual autonomy in work arrangement vs. collective visibility and systemic resilience
summary: Help people work flexibly while keeping the team coordinated and secure. Balance individual needs with what the organization can actually support.

title: Managing Divided Loyalties in Business
tension: Insider access & legitimate self-interest vs. fiduciary duty & systemic integrity
summary: When someone has obligations to multiple groups at once, how do you keep things fair? This pattern shows how to disclose conflicts, recuse people when needed, and keep everyone accountable.

title: Managing Money Across Borders
tension: Centrifugal fragmentation (each currency zone operating in isolation, hidden exposure, opaque conversion) vs. Centripetal coherence (flows visible, rates locked predictably, settlement synchronized across zones)
summary: Handle currency exchanges fairly and transparently across your network. Lock in rates, track exposure, and settle accounts so everyone knows what's happening.

title: Managing Money Between Companies
tension: Efficiency of consolidated flows vs. clarity of individual contribution and settlement
summary: How to move payments between separate legal entities smoothly while keeping everyone accountable and reducing unnecessary friction.

title: Managing Money Between Company Units
tension: Internal coherence vs. external legitimacy — the need to move resources, costs, and profits between legal entities while keeping the whole system coherent for consolidated reporting and tax authorities.
summary: When you have multiple companies working together, you need fair prices for internal transactions and clean accounting that satisfies tax authorities and stakeholders.

title: Managing Risk With Your Vendors
tension: Autonomy & Control vs. Interdependence & Trust
summary: Build real trust with vendors by staying on top of what they do for you, what they cost, and what you depend on them for. Regular check-ins and honest conversations keep these partnerships healthy.

title: Managing Shared Hardware from Start to End
tension: Linear consumption (buy-use-discard) vs. cyclical stewardship (acquire-deploy-refresh-restore)
summary: Track what you own, know where it is, and retire it responsibly. Good hardware stewardship keeps costs visible and makes sure nothing gets lost or wasted.

title: Managing Time as a Business Tool
tension: Rigid enforcement (brittleness, harm on expired crossing) vs. permissive neglect (degradation, liability, customer confusion)
summary: Treat deadlines and expiration dates as living guides, not rigid walls. Build systems that give you early warning and adapt when timing matters.

title: Managing Work When Everything Depends on Everything
tension: Abundance of strategic intent vs. scarcity of execution capacity
summary: Coordinate strategic initiatives across your organization by making trade-offs visible and deciding them transparently, rather than letting politics determine what gets done when.

title: Managing Your Business Portfolio
tension: Coherence vs. Autonomy: How to govern a portfolio as a unified living system while preserving the adaptive capacity of semi-autonomous units.
summary: Balance multiple business lines like a gardener tends different plants. Each needs the right resources, honest feedback about how it's doing, and willingness to shift investment when conditions change.

title: Map Your Life to Find What Matters
tension: Fragmentation vs. Coherence: Life compartmentalizes into isolated domains (work, health, relationships, growth, community) while the self seeks integration; yet premature integration through false models imprisons more than it liberates.
summary: Regularly chart how you're doing across different areas of life—work, relationships, health, growth—to spot patterns and imbalances. Use the map as a guide, not gospel.

title: Mapping Access and Shared Urban Space
tension: Coherence vs. Diversity — how to maintain a unified commons that serves radically different needs without forcing homogeneity or fragmenting into incompatible sub-systems.
summary: Create flexible boundary systems and access levels so different groups can share the same urban area without conflicts, each getting what they need from the commons.

title: Marking Endings That Matter
tension: Unprocessed endings (accumulating as emotional weight, institutional amnesia, and fragmented identities) vs. Ritualized closure (creating completion, extracting learning, and enabling regeneration)
summary: Ritual and ceremony transform how we end things—relationships, projects, roles, life chapters. They help us extract meaning, honor what was, and genuinely move forward instead of just abandoning the past.

title: Marking Life's Turning Points
tension: Continuous time vs. discontinuous transformation
summary: Create rituals and visible markers for life's big changes—coming of age, loss, new beginnings. This transforms time into meaning and helps us move forward with intention.

title: Marking Life's Turning Points
tension: Continuous time vs. discontinuous transformation
summary: Create rituals and visible markers for life's big changes—coming of age, loss, new beginnings. This transforms time into meaning and helps us move forward with intention.

title: Marking Moments That Matter
tension: Procedural governance (rules, decisions, efficiency) vs. Relational governance (meaning, belonging, sacred obligation)
summary: Cities use ceremonies and rituals to define boundaries, build community identity, and make governance feel meaningful. These shared moments create belonging and signal what a place values.

title: Marking Moments That Matter
tension: Procedural governance (rules, decisions, efficiency) vs. Relational governance (meaning, belonging, sacred obligation)
summary: Cities use ceremonies and rituals to define boundaries, build community identity, and make governance feel meaningful. These shared moments create belonging and signal what a place values.

title: Matching Animals to Land's Capacity
tension: Herd productivity vs. pasture recovery | Fixed quotas vs. adaptive responsiveness | Individual grazing pressure vs. commons resilience
summary: Keep livestock numbers in sync with what the land can actually support. Monitor conditions and adjust together, so herds and pasture both thrive.

title: Matching Animals to What They Eat
tension: Nutritional adequacy of animals vs. regenerative capacity of forage systems
summary: Track how nutritious your pasture is across seasons so your livestock stay healthy and your land stays fertile. Simple monitoring practices that help you make better grazing decisions.

title: Matching Money to Reality
tension: Fidelity to economic reality vs. certainty of timing—how to recognize value in the period it is earned or incurred, when invoices, payments, and actual costs arrive asynchronously.
summary: Record income and expenses when they actually happen, not just when cash moves. It's how you keep your books honest and spot problems early.

title: Matching Service Demand with Available Time
tension: Predictable service delivery vs. adaptive response to emergent demand and human variability
summary: Coordinate when customers need service with when your team can deliver it. Good scheduling keeps people from waiting and your team from overload.

title: Measure What Actually Changed
tension: Claiming necessary credit vs. overclaiming in complex systems; Transparency vs. reductive simplification
summary: Track your real impact honestly—what you touched, what you caused, what went wrong—and answer to the people affected, not just the money.

title: Measure What Actually Matters
tension: What gets measured vs. what matters | Accountability that clarifies vs. accountability that distorts
summary: Build measurement systems that track real outcomes, not just convenient numbers. Keep metrics honest, resist gaming, and let them evolve as you learn what works.

title: Measure What Nature Actually Does
tension: Biodiversity presence vs. biodiversity function
summary: Stop counting species and start measuring whether ecosystems are doing their job. When you link biodiversity to real functions—pollination, water cycling, pest control—you can spot problems before they spiral.

title: Measure Your Body's Real Age
tension: Chronological age vs. biological capacity — treating time's passage as inevitable decline vs. recognizing that physiological function can be monitored, influenced, and restored
summary: Track the biological signals that reveal how your body is actually aging, then use that feedback to make changes that extend healthy years, not just calendar years.

title: Measuring How Nature Bounces Back
tension: Knowing how much change a living system can survive vs. acting decisively within that threshold without paralysis or false precision.
summary: Understand what your ecosystem can handle—shocks, stress, change—then govern and use it within those limits. The difference between thriving systems and broken ones.

title: Measuring Nature's Real Recovery
tension: Accountability for ecosystem restoration vs. adaptive response to ecological complexity and uncertainty
summary: Track what actually happens to wildlife and ecosystems over time, adjust your conservation work as you learn, and stay honest about whether you're truly helping nature heal.

title: Measuring Soil's Living Breath
tension: Carbon as invisible flux vs. Carbon as stewarded, knowable flow
summary: Track how soil microbes release carbon into the air. Regular monitoring reveals whether your land is building or losing fertility.

title: Measuring What Actually Heals
tension: Proving regeneration works vs. learning how regeneration actually works in place
summary: Track real changes in ecosystem health through cycles of practice and learning that strengthen both land and people, from individual stewards to whole regions.

title: Measuring What Actually Matters
tension: Accountability (demonstrating real change to all stakeholders) vs. Adaptation (staying alive to emergent reality and unintended consequences)
summary: Move beyond vanity metrics to real measurement that involves everyone affected, stays honest about what you've actually changed, and evolves instead of becoming a game.

title: Measuring What Actually Matters for the Planet
tension: Declared sustainability commitments vs. measured ecological reality
summary: Build real accountability for environmental impact through honest measurement, adaptive financing, and governance that keeps your organization answerable to actual ecological limits—not sustainability marketing.

title: Measuring What Actually Matters
tension: Quantifiable proxy metrics vs. actual lived outcomes; external expert judgment vs. community-defined success; false certainty vs. honest uncertainty
summary: Build ways to track impact that capture justice and real change, not just what's easy to count. Listen to communities and get comfortable with uncertainty.

title: Measuring What Actually Matters
tension: Quantifiable proxy metrics vs. actual lived outcomes; external expert judgment vs. community-defined success; false certainty vs. honest uncertainty
summary: Build ways to track impact that capture justice and real change, not just what's easy to count. Listen to communities and get comfortable with uncertainty.

title: Meeting People Where They Are
tension: Broadcast clarity vs. Audience readiness | Signal fidelity vs. Channel adaptation | Personal integrity vs. Contextual belonging
summary: Shape your message to fit who you're talking to, when they're ready to listen, and where they'll actually see it. Respect what matters to them, and they'll hear you.

title: Mending What Breaks in Relationships
tension: Attachment vs. Authenticity — the pull to preserve connection at any cost versus the requirement to honor truth about what serves all participants.
summary: Relationships need care to survive conflict and harm. Learn to assess damage honestly, repair what matters, and decide what's worth saving.

title: Messages Find Their Own Way
tension: Autonomy of distributed agents vs. coherence of the whole system
summary: Build systems where services talk to each other honestly about what they can handle, so information flows smoothly without a central boss deciding everything.

title: Mixing Income Levels in Neighborhoods
tension: Zoning as wealth concentration (exclusionary, tenure-segregated, fiscally captured) vs. zoning as commons stewardship (integrated, tenure-diverse, metropolitan equitable)
summary: Use zoning rules to require mixed-income housing in new developments, so affordable and market-rate homes exist side by side instead of separated by neighborhood.

title: Money Flows Like a Living Thing
tension: Immediate survival vs. intergenerational thriving
summary: Plan your finances so your organization stays healthy today and survives tomorrow. Show where money goes, adjust as you learn, and care for people along the way.

title: Money Governance That Honors Relationships
tension: Individual autonomy vs. relational interdependence — the need to honor separate agency while acknowledging shared fate
summary: Design financial systems that keep autonomy and interdependence in balance, turn hidden agreements into clear conversations, and use transparency as care, not control.

title: Money That Builds Trust
tension: Revenue concentration (extraction) vs. revenue circulation (regeneration)
summary: Design how you make money so it strengthens relationships, shares value fairly, and stays transparent. This creates real stability that survives market shifts.

title: Money That Flows to Everyone
tension: Extraction (value concentrates in ownership layers) vs. Regeneration (value circulates through all participants)
summary: Design financial systems where profits, information, and decisions move through all stakeholders instead of concentrating at the top. Capital regenerates value rather than extracting it.

title: Money That Heals the Land
tension: Short-term extraction vs. long-term regeneration — between taking value from commons and building value back into them
summary: Design finances so that profit from healthy ecosystems flows back into restoration and community capacity. Align what you earn with what you regenerate.

title: Money That Moves Through Trust
tension: Centralized financial gatekeeping vs. distributed financial stewardship
summary: How groups can manage and share financial resources fairly, letting people who've been left out by banks participate, borrow, and have a say in how money flows.

title: Money That Moves Together
tension: Individual survival vs. collective resilience; capital scarcity vs. cooperative abundance; crisis as collapse vs. crisis as threshold for transformation.
summary: Cooperatives pool resources to help members through tough times and fund ownership transitions. One cooperative's strength becomes another's safety net.

title: Money That Moves With Real Life
tension: Participatory capital mobilization vs. retail participant protection from currency, timing, and redemption risks they cannot control or hedge
summary: Design local currencies and financing tools that sync with how people actually earn and spend, so communities can trade and invest without running out of cash or trust.

title: Money That Moves With Your Life
tension: Financial security vs. life autonomy — the need to sustain material survival while preserving freedom to change direction, care for others, face illness, and age without compulsion.
summary: Build financial systems that give people real choices through major life changes—health crises, aging, career shifts—so survival doesn't dictate who they are.

title: Money That Respects Your Mission
tension: Growth requires external capital infusion vs. capital infusion threatens distributed governance and long-term stewardship
summary: How to raise and manage capital without losing control of your organization's direction and values.

title: Money Through Life's Big Changes
tension: Long-term financial security vs. present agency and adaptability; rigid planning vs. living responsively to change
summary: Plan your finances for what's actually coming—retirement, career shifts, health changes—so you stay secure without losing control of your choices.

title: Moving Animals Through Land and Time
tension: Productivity vs. Regeneration — how to extract value (forage, meat, fertility) without degrading the living systems that enable extraction
summary: Rotate livestock across land in patterns that let soil and plants recover, turning grazing into something that rebuilds rather than depletes the land.

title: Moving Freely Through Our Cities
tension: Hyperregulated, surveilled, sedentary urban space vs. free, diverse, stable embodied movement anchored in place and culture
summary: Everyone deserves safe, accessible ways to get around. We explore how cities can reduce mobility barriers and stress while ensuring all people—regardless of ability or income—can move freely and independently.

title: Moving Herds to Let Land Recover
tension: Forage yield vs. grassland regeneration
summary: Move livestock between pastures on a schedule that matches plant growth and soil needs, so land gets time to bounce back. It builds healthier soil and more productive grazing over time.

title: Moving the City After Dark
tension: Institutional schedules (fixed, peak-centered, convenient for planners) vs. lived temporal reality (shift work, care obligations, irregular rhythms, concentrated among low-wage workers)
summary: Shift workers design their own transit and scheduling systems instead of fitting into schedules built for 9-to-5. Fair access to getting around and getting rest, any hour of the day.

title: Moving Through Loss Without Getting Stuck
tension: Acknowledging genuine loss (which requires stopping, naming, feeling) vs. moving forward (which requires releasing, adapting, rebuilding)—without rushing either process or collapsing one into the other.
summary: How to process grief and change so sorrow doesn't turn into bitterness or despair. A practice for navigating loss across all parts of life—work, identity, relationships, abilities.

title: Moving Together Builds Resilience
tension: Disembodiment (cognitive abstraction, trauma freeze, digital dominance) vs. Embodied Aliveness (somatic intelligence, nervous system capacity, creative presence)
summary: When we move, craft, and practice together—whether dancing, meditating, or healing—we regulate our nervous systems and strengthen our relationships. The body becomes a shared resource for wellbeing and creativity.

title: Name Your Feelings, Change Your Story
tension: Emotional diffusion & reactivity vs. emotional granularity & conscious choice
summary: When people develop precise language for their emotions and body sensations, they become more aware of unconscious patterns and can make better decisions together. It's foundational to how groups actually work.

title: Nature's Senses in the City
tension: Abstraction & Distance vs. Sensory Presence & Attentiveness
summary: Use sensory experiences and biophilic design to reconnect people with ecosystems while monitoring environmental health through natural perception.

title: Navigate Tax Obligations Across Borders
tension: Fragmented, hidden tax obligations (legal/financial risk, opacity, unfairness) vs. Integrated, visible tax stewardship (adaptive capacity, equitable contribution, systemic resilience)
summary: Master tax provisions, withholding calculations, and multi-jurisdiction requirements to keep your business compliant and audit-ready.

title: Navigating Inner Shifts Safely
tension: Expansion vs. Integrity: The drive to explore consciousness deeply and authentically vs. the requirement to remain grounded, safe, and coherent across all self-states and contexts.
summary: How to explore consciousness and altered states with intention and stability—building safety practices, tracking what changes in you, and staying integrated through transformation.

title: Neighborhood Childcare Pods
tension: Childcare as privatized household burden (isolating parents, precarious workers, invisible children) vs. childcare as shared commons stewardship (distributing care responsibility, enabling participation, building neighbourhood resilience)
summary: Communities pool resources to create affordable, locally-run childcare in homes and shared spaces, strengthening both child development and neighborhood bonds.

title: Neighborhood Pharmacies Leading Community Care
tension: Fragmented, institution-dependent care vs. integrated, community-rooted health stewardship
summary: Pharmacies team up with local clinics to make medications affordable and catch health problems early through accessible community screening.

title: Neighborhoods Own Their Own Data
tension: Individual privacy & autonomy vs. collective verification & service access
summary: A neighborhood collectively manages residents' digital identities—each person holds the keys to their own data while the city verifies who they are. This unlocks access to services and economic opportunity without surveillance or corporate control.

title: Neighborhoods Taking Care of Water Together
tension: Centralised, hidden water infrastructure (fragile, inequitable, unintelligible) vs. Distributed, visible, community-governed water systems (resilient, just, generative)
summary: Communities govern and maintain their own water systems—from collecting rainwater to treating it—building skills and security while sharing the work.

title: Neighborhoods That Do More Than One Thing
tension: Homogenization (single-use creep, commercial strips, residential monoculture) vs. Polyculture (fine-grained mixing, live-work integration, ground-floor diversity)
summary: Zoning that mixes homes, shops, and workspaces together so neighborhoods stay alive, diverse, and resilient instead of turning into one-purpose zones.

title: Neighborhoods That Heal Equitably
tension: Centralized health systems that reproduce structural racism vs. Community-rooted governance that names and repairs inequities at their source
summary: A system where communities design and govern health services together, addressing the root causes that make some neighborhoods healthier than others.

title: Neighborhoods That Warn Each Other
tension: Technical hazard data (invisible to most residents, concentrated in distant systems) vs. lived neighborhood knowledge (fragmented, uncoordinated, inaccessible to decision-makers)
summary: Communities create their own early warning systems and safe routes so everyone—regardless of language or ability—knows what's coming and where to go when disaster strikes.

title: Neighbors Growing Food Together
tension: Capital access vs. community ownership | Individual enterprise vs. collective resilience
summary: Communities own and share kitchen and growing spaces, so local food producers can start businesses without huge upfront costs while keeping profits in the neighborhood.

title: Neighbors Pooling Money for Housing Stability
tension: Individual financial vulnerability vs. collective capacity to absorb shocks without debt or dispossession
summary: Residents contribute regularly to community funds they control together, creating an emergency safety net that prevents eviction, covers repair costs, and keeps people housed without credit checks or outside lenders.

title: Neighbors Supporting Each Other's Mental Health
tension: Professional clinical authority vs. peer solidarity and survivor knowledge; institutional crisis response vs. community-rooted healing; mental health as individual pathology vs. mental health as relational commons
summary: People with lived experience of mental health struggles lead their own support networks, create jobs, and shape how care works in their communities.

title: Neighbors Supporting Neighbors Housing
tension: Individual housing precarity vs. collective housing resilience; mobility needs vs. affordability preservation; survival outside market/state vs. institutionalization that enables scale
summary: Communities unite through shared housing resources, peer exchanges, and mutual support networks that keep people stably housed and rooted in their neighborhoods.

title: Neighbors Watching Out for Health Threats
tension: Early detection vs. equitable response | Centralized expertise vs. distributed trust
summary: Train community members to spot emerging health and environmental dangers early—from disease outbreaks to dangerous heat—then act fast together. It builds trust while keeping everyone safer.

title: Neighbours Sharing the Work of Care
tension: Care as invisible, individualised burden (leading to burnout, exploitation, isolation) vs. Care as visible, distributed, collectively-stewarded commonwealth (building resilience, dignity, and interdependence)
summary: Care workers, family caregivers, and neighbours pool resources and rotate duties to prevent burnout, protect each other's right to say no, and make caregiving a shared responsibility instead of an individual struggle.

title: Never Let a Contract Slip Away
tension: Invisible expiry dates + concentrated renewal responsibility vs. Distributed stewardship + advance visibility
summary: Make contracts visible across your organization so nothing expires unnoticed, renewals happen at the right time, and responsibility is shared so critical agreements stay active.

title: Never Let Credentials Expire
tension: Trust decay (credentials lapse, authority evaporates, compliance collapses) vs. Continuous stewardship (credentials renewed before threshold, authority transferred before expiration, compliance maintained as living practice)
summary: Track certificates, permits, and certifications so renewals happen on time and nothing lapses. Visibility and automation turn compliance from chaos into routine.

title: Numbers That Tell the Truth
tension: Signal clarity vs. Signal distortion — the practitioner's need for honest diagnosis vs. the system's gravitational pull toward comforting narratives
summary: Stop chasing vanity metrics. Track what actually matters—cash flow, capacity limits, real health—so you see problems coming before they hit.

title: Open Government by Design
tension: Information asymmetry (those with power withhold reasoning & data) vs. distributed knowledge (all stewards visible, all flows traceable, all decisions explainable)
summary: Cities that require public disclosure of budgets, decisions, and operations build trust and enable residents to hold officials accountable through accessible, cascading oversight systems.

title: Operating Within Earth's Limits
tension: Local autonomy and regeneration ambition vs. planetary boundary compliance and biophysical limits
summary: Design local practices that respect planetary boundaries by defining safe operating spaces, monitoring them, and learning when we're pushing too hard.

title: Own What You Make, Forever
tension: Externalizing end-of-life costs (linear take-make-waste) vs. Internalizing responsibility and value recovery (cyclical stewardship)
summary: Take responsibility for your product from creation through disposal. Build systems that let you see what happens at every stage and capture value by designing things that regenerate instead of harm.

title: Ownership That Serves Your Mission
tension: Profit maximization vs. multi-stakeholder stewardship / Centralized control vs. distributed governance / Short-term extraction vs. long-term mission persistence
summary: Structure your enterprise so multiple stakeholders share power and profit, locking in your values legally so extractive forces can't take over.

title: Owning Your Cloud Without Getting Locked In
tension: Velocity & Abstraction vs. Visibility & Autonomy
summary: Build cloud systems you actually control. Make what's happening visible, distribute decision-making, and design ways to leave whenever you need to—so technology stays a tool, not a trap.

title: Owning Your Data, Protecting Your Privacy
tension: Autonomy vs. Interdependence — the pull between reclaiming control over personal information and recognizing that data about you affects those connected to you
summary: Take real control of your personal information—deciding what you share, with whom, and why. Protect what matters while understanding how your data affects others.

title: Owning Your Platform, Planning Your Exit
tension: Platform dependency (convenience, reach, network effects) vs. Commons autonomy (ownership, governance, continuity)
summary: Build real community ownership of your platform while keeping the ability to leave. Your work and relationships should survive any single platform's collapse.

title: Packaging That Actually Comes Back
tension: Linear extraction & disposal vs. cyclical regeneration & stewardship
summary: Choose materials wisely, design them to be reused or safely returned to nature, and measure what actually matters. Turn packaging from trash into something that cycles endlessly.

title: Passing Down Cooperative Wealth
tension: Accumulation vs. Circulation: Early members build real wealth; later members face steep entry costs and exclusion. Yet distributing all surplus immediately starves long-term resilience. The tension is between rewarding contribution and keeping the commons alive for newcomers.
summary: How cooperatives share accumulated wealth fairly across generations—through thoughtful vesting, surplus decisions, and democratic inheritance—so advantage doesn't get hoarded or extracted.

title: Passing Down Local Businesses to the Next Generation
tension: Founder exit (retirement, death, transition) vs. community asset preservation — extraction of value to departing owner vs. stewardship of enterprise as shared livelihood commons
summary: When local business owners step back, how do their enterprises, knowledge, and wealth stay in the community? A guided process that keeps livelihoods alive and wealth local across generations.

title: Passing Down Money and Values
tension: Wealth as private accumulation vs. wealth as shared stewardship; knowledge hoarded vs. knowledge transmitted; entitlement vs. capable inheritance
summary: Help your wealth serve what matters most across generations. Combine thoughtful planning with conversations that build financial understanding and shared purpose in your family.

title: Passing Down What Matters
tension: Knowledge loss vs. living transmission | Age segregation vs. intergenerational kinship | Inherited wisdom vs. emergent innovation
summary: Create ways for elders to share their knowledge and values with younger generations, building stronger relationships and ensuring wisdom doesn't get lost.

title: Passing Knowledge Forward
tension: Knowledge trapped in individual minds & tacit practice vs. Knowledge stewarded as shared commons
summary: How communities document what they know so others can learn it, build on it, and keep it alive. A practice of care that turns experience into something real and shareable.

title: Passing Land Forward: Building Young Farmer Futures
tension: Short-term extraction vs. intergenerational cultivation; individual ownership vs. community authorization; knowledge loss vs. transmission across time.
summary: Help young farmers gain land access and skills through mentorship, inheritance planning, and orchards that thrive across generations.

title: Passing Leadership to the Next Generation
tension: Concentration of authority in a departing leader vs. distributed, living capacity to sustain shared purpose across transitions
summary: Build trusted successors while you lead, so your organization stays strong when leadership changes hands. This keeps knowledge and values alive beyond any one person.

title: Passing On a Thriving Business
tension: Maximizing exit valuation vs. preserving the commons embedded in the enterprise
summary: How to transition your enterprise to new stewards in ways that preserve its values, finances, and mission—so it keeps contributing rather than getting stripped for profit.

title: Passing On What Matters
tension: Mortality vs. Continuity — the finite self must choose what persists beyond its own span.
summary: Write down your values and stories so the people you care about know what mattered to you. A way to steward what you want remembered.

title: Passing On What We Know
tension: Founder indispensability & knowledge enclosure vs. distributed stewardship & institutional resilience
summary: Build systems to share governance knowledge and relationships across your team so no one person is irreplaceable. Protect your organization from founder dependency and ensure smooth transitions.

title: Passing On What You Know
tension: Self-focused accumulation vs. Other-oriented stewardship
summary: Create real ways for experienced people to share their wisdom and resources with the next generation. It's how communities stay alive across time.

title: Passing the Baton Without Breaking It
tension: Extraction vs. Regeneration — the pull to maximize individual exit value vs. the responsibility to ensure the system survives and thrives beyond the founder's departure.
summary: How to hand over a business to the next generation or owner while keeping relationships intact, protecting everyone involved, and making sure the mission survives the handoff.

title: Passing the Torch Without Breaking It
tension: Founder indispensability vs. institutional resilience; knowledge hoarding vs. generative handoff; crisis transition vs. graceful evolution
summary: Plan for leadership transitions as natural evolution, not crisis. Build distributed leadership and knowledge sharing so your organization thrives long after founders leave.

title: Passing Work Forward Without Losing Ground
tension: Continuity of care vs. discontinuity of presence—how to maintain stewardship when the steward changes.
summary: How to hand off people, systems, and knowledge between shifts so nothing falls through the cracks. The goal: keep everyone safe, maintain quality, and preserve what matters most.

title: Pause and Choose Again
tension: Obligation (continuing by inertia) vs. Consent (continuing by choice)
summary: Regular rituals where people consciously recommit to their group, turning duty into genuine choice and catching problems before they grow.

title: Pause Before You React
tension: Automaticity vs. Awareness — the gap between reactive habit and reflective agency
summary: Build moments of awareness into your automatic habits—whether emotional, competitive, relational, or attentional—so you can choose your response instead of just reacting.

title: Pause Between Feeling and Doing
tension: Automaticity vs. Conscious Choice — the gap between reactive impulse and deliberate action aligned with stated values.
summary: Create space to notice what you're feeling and choose how to respond. Treat emotions as useful signals, not commands you have to follow.

title: Pay People to Heal the City
tension: Ecological regeneration work vs. precarious, extractive labor | Environmental commons stewardship vs. fragmented private contracts | Knowledge transfer across generations vs. skill loss
summary: Create good-paying jobs in nature repair—tree care, stream restoration, green infrastructure—run as worker cooperatives where people learn skills, earn fair wages, and have a say in their work.

title: Paying Back What We Owe the Land
tension: Invisible ecological harm (degradation treated as externality) vs. Visible reciprocal obligation (damage quantified as debt owed to land and future stewards)
summary: A system for measuring environmental damage as real debts, then distributing restoration work fairly across generations to rebuild our relationship with nature.

title: Paying Farmers for the Switch
tension: Immediate financial survival vs. long-term ecological regeneration
summary: Help farmers move to regenerative practices without going broke. Redesign subsidies and support systems to cover real transition costs and reward long-term soil health instead of extraction.

title: Paying for Nature to Heal
tension: Restoration needs perpetual funding and oversight vs. Grant cycles are temporary and incentivize short-term extraction
summary: Design financial systems that fund ecological restoration and keep it going for generations, with clear accountability and community control over the money.

title: Paying for What the Land Provides
tension: Invisible ecological value vs. visible financial accounting; individual service optimization vs. systemic trade-off navigation
summary: Track what ecosystems actually produce—clean water, stored carbon, pollination—and reward the people who keep them healthy. Make nature's contributions visible so stewardship gets funded.

title: Paying People to Protect Nature
tension: Individual economic survival vs. collective ecological regeneration
summary: Align money with conservation by rewarding those who protect ecosystems and making those who harm them pay. When stewardship pays and damage costs something, people choose differently.

title: Paying People to Protect Nature
tension: Individual economic survival vs. collective ecological regeneration
summary: Align money with conservation by rewarding those who protect ecosystems and making those who harm them pay. When stewardship pays and damage costs something, people choose differently.

title: Phasing Out Farm Chemical Pollution
tension: Chemical efficacy vs. ecological integrity: using synthetics to suppress pests/weeds while keeping cumulative toxin burden below the threshold where food webs and soil biology collapse.
summary: Monitor where farm chemicals settle and persist, set safe limits for ecosystems, then systematically eliminate them. Keeps soil, water, and food webs healthy.

title: Pilgrimage as Coming Home Changed
tension: Rootedness vs. Exploration — the false choice between belonging to place and encountering the world. True pilgrimage holds both: cycles of departure and return that deepen relationship to home while expanding perspective.
summary: Travel that transforms you—deepening your connection to places and people, then bringing that wisdom back to your own community. The opposite of tourism.

title: Plan for Drought Before It Arrives
tension: Prediction vs. Adaptation — we cannot know exactly when drought will strike or how severe it will be, yet we must commit reserves and rules now, without waste during abundant years.
summary: Set up early warning systems and contingency rules so you manage water scarcity gradually instead of facing sudden crisis. Know your thresholds, keep reserves ready, and adjust allocations before you run dry.

title: Plan What Happens to Your Life's Work
tension: Intention vs. Abandonment — the gap between what you want to leave behind and what actually survives you because it was never made visible, accessible, or living.
summary: Document your assets, data, and values. Choose who'll care for them. Update your plan each year as your life changes.

title: Plan Your Crisis Before It Hits
tension: Preparation vs. Paralysis: Over-planning for crises that may never come, versus being utterly unprepared when they do arrive.
summary: Design your emergency response when things are calm, so you can act decisively instead of panicking when crisis strikes. Test it beforehand.

title: Plan Your Life Multiple Ways
tension: Single-path planning (illusory certainty, brittle) vs. Multi-scenario stewardship (acknowledged uncertainty, adaptive)
summary: Imagine different futures for yourself and prepare for them now. It builds real resilience by helping you stay flexible and ready for what comes.

title: Plan Your Own Death
tension: Autonomy vs. Incapacity — the gap between who you are now (capable of choice) and who you may become (unable to speak for yourself). Fill that gap proactively, or let crisis and strangers fill it for you.
summary: Say what matters to you about dying, choose who decides for you, and talk about it now. Stay in control when it counts most.

title: Planning for Climate-Ready Cities and People
tension: Adaptation-driven displacement vs. adaptation-as-commons stewardship
summary: Help cities prepare for climate migration by building inclusive reception systems, preventing displacement, and strengthening community-led resilience that keeps neighborhoods intact.

title: Planning for Multiple Ecological Futures
tension: Single predicted future vs. multiple plausible pathways; planning confidence vs. adaptive readiness
summary: Work through different possible ecological futures together to test your governance and land stewardship decisions before crisis hits, building the flexibility to adapt.

title: Planning When You Have Less Than Enough
tension: Demand growth vs. Capacity limits
summary: Figure out what work actually fits with the people and time you have, then adjust as you learn what really happens versus what you predicted.

title: Play Builds Trust and Belonging
tension: Play as frivolous escape vs. Play as essential social technology for building trust, testing limits, and transmitting culture
summary: Create spaces where people play together to build trust, work through conflict, explore who they are, and pass on what matters. Play strengthens communities from the inside out.

title: Play to Your Strengths, Know Your Limits
tension: Self-knowledge (honest inventory of what you are) vs. Self-design (intentional structuring of where that self operates)
summary: Figure out what you're genuinely good at and where you hit your ceiling, then build roles around your strengths instead of fixing weaknesses.

title: Playing Fair in the City
tension: Sport as commodity (extracted, enclosed, elite-serving) vs. sport as commons (regenerative, stewarded, community-rooted)
summary: Create accessible sports spaces for all neighborhoods while protecting communities from displacement and supporting grassroots athletes and informal sports economies.

title: Polluters Fund What Communities Choose to Fix
tension: Polluter escape (externalizing costs to future generations) vs. community stewardship (restoring what was degraded, choosing how)
summary: Communities harmed by pollution decide how cleanup money gets spent, with independent checks ensuring the work actually happens before companies escape liability.

title: Power Closest to the People
tension: Local autonomy and face-to-face accountability vs. coordination capacity and systemic resilience across metropolitan scales
summary: Let communities make decisions at their own level, then connect them fairly—so neighborhoods stay in control while staying accountable to each other.

title: Power That Doesn't Break When One Part Fails
tension: Concentration of authority vs. fragmentation of accountability — between the efficiency of centralised decision-making and the resilience of distributed, overlapping governance.
summary: Spread decision-making and control across multiple groups and levels so no single actor becomes a bottleneck. When one part breaks, the whole system keeps working.

title: Practice What You Actually Believe
tension: Inner fragmentation (competing intentions, cognitive overload, disconnection from body and reality) vs. Integrated presence (coherent values, embodied commitment, reliable self-knowledge)
summary: Close the gap between what you intend and what you do through regular practice cycles that combine clear thinking, body awareness, and real-world testing.

title: Practice Your Emergency Plan Before You Need It
tension: Theoretical preparedness vs. proven capability—the gap between documented procedures and their actual execution under stress.
summary: Run regular drills and test your backups so when disaster strikes, your team knows exactly what to do. Preparation turns survival from theory into muscle memory.

title: Prepare for Multiple Futures
tension: Preparing for uncertainty without pretending to predict it
summary: Test your assumptions and develop backup plans by exploring different scenarios, so your commons can adapt quickly when conditions change instead of getting caught off guard.

title: Preparing for Business Seasons
tension: Predictable cyclical demand vs. the temptation to build permanent excess capacity or let troughs starve the operation.
summary: Anticipate busy and slow periods, then adjust your resources, inventory, and pricing to handle peaks without waste or strain during troughs.

title: Preserving History, Enabling Change
tension: Preservation vs. Vitality: heritage buildings face obsolescence if locked into single uses, yet demolition erases embodied knowledge and place identity. Adaptive reuse requires zoning flexibility, but unfettered conversion risks losing character and displacing communities.
summary: Streamline zoning rules and interior flexibility to make heritage building reuse faster and more feasible, while protecting materials and character.

title: Preserving Stories That Make Us
tension: Institutional gatekeeping of collective memory vs. community authority over documentation, access, and interpretation
summary: Communities document and digitize their own histories—from factory floors to family memories—ensuring local voices shape the archive rather than outsiders.

title: Price as a Signal of Real Value
tension: Capturing sufficient value to sustain the system vs. preserving participant agency and fairness in exchange
summary: Set prices so they show what people actually care about, spread costs fairly, and keep the system healthy without anyone extracting excess value.

title: Pricing That Reflects Real Value
tension: Revenue extraction (maximizing what we take) vs. Value stewardship (ensuring price reflects worth and serves all participants justly)
summary: Set prices to show what you're actually delivering, share gains fairly with everyone involved, and explain your logic so people trust the exchange is fair.

title: Protect Culture Before Gentrification Hits
tension: Cultural vitality as attractor vs. cultural displacement as consequence; market value creation vs. community stewardship; aesthetic preservation vs. living culture maintenance
summary: Use zoning rules tied to affordable housing and community control to keep cultural spaces alive as neighborhoods change. Culture attracts investment—but investment often kills the culture that made it attractive.

title: Protect Ideas While They Grow
tension: Protecting vulnerable emergence vs. exposing work to public scrutiny and iteration
summary: Create safe spaces where creative work can develop naturally, shielded from criticism and pressure until it's ready. Sometimes good ideas need time before the world sees them.

title: Protect the Species That Hold Everything Together
tension: Abundance vs. Consequence — the species that matters least by biomass often matters most by ecosystem function.
summary: Some species have outsized power—their loss would unravel an entire ecosystem. Find them, understand what they do, and make sure they survive.

title: Protect Your Attention Like a Shared Resource
tension: Autonomy of attention vs. Always-on expectation
summary: Set clear rules for when people can reach you and how. Design your notifications and availability around what matters to you, not what apps push by default.

title: Protect Your Creative Work
tension: Creative authenticity & meaning-making vs. economic viability & market visibility
summary: Keep your art or craft thriving by building identity, finding income, sharing your process, and staying inspired—without letting money demands destroy what makes it meaningful.

title: Protect Your Energy for What Matters
tension: Decision fatigue (degraded judgment from choice overload) vs. preserving cognitive energy for high-leverage choices
summary: Stop wasting mental energy on small decisions. Automate the trivial stuff, tackle big choices when you're fresh, and build in time to recover so you can focus on what actually counts.

title: Protect Your Energy Like a Commons
tension: Reactive urgency vs. intentional stewardship of finite life energy
summary: Your time and energy are finite resources worth protecting. Learn to forecast what you can handle, prioritize what matters, let go of what's draining, and build recovery into your rhythm.

title: Protect Your Mental Energy
tension: Cognitive abundance (surplus capacity available for learning, adaptation, judgment) vs. Cognitive depletion (overload that collapses decision quality, resilience, and the ability to respond to emergence)
summary: Your mind needs rhythm like your body needs sleep. Measure what drains you, build in recovery time, and hand off routine tasks so you stay sharp and creative.

title: Protecting and Sharing Plant Medicine Knowledge
tension: Knowledge preservation vs. Knowledge appropriation; Ecological regeneration vs. Resource depletion; Cultural continuity vs. Intergenerational rupture
summary: Keep medicinal plant wisdom alive by documenting it, growing the plants responsibly, and deciding together who can use and benefit from this knowledge—without letting outsiders exploit it.

title: Protecting and Sharing What You Know
tension: Knowledge assets are simultaneously fragile (easily copied, boundary-blurred, jurisdiction-dependent) and foundational (they generate disproportionate value). Yet treating them as static inventory disconnects from the living, relational nature of how ideas move, combine, and create meaning across an interconnected ecosystem.
summary: Track what your organization knows and owns, manage who can use it, and keep everything current as your business grows. Covers patents, trademarks, licenses, and who holds what rights.

title: Protecting Animals That Cross Borders
tension: Ecological continuity vs. political fragmentation — species move across borders; governance stops at them.
summary: When species migrate across regions, protection efforts need to work together. This means coordinating across boundaries to manage movement, invasive species, and habitat corridors so animals can survive.

title: Protecting Attention as a Shared Resource
tension: Cognitive capacity as scarce commons vs. attention fragmentation as default entropy
summary: Your attention is worth protecting—for yourself and everyone around you. Build focus through embodied practices, thoughtful environments, and rhythms that respect both work and rest.

title: Protecting Birds on Their Journey
tension: Fragmented intervention (point fixes at breeding or wintering grounds) vs. systemic stewardship (continuous flow across the complete migration cycle)
summary: Help migratory species complete their annual routes by mapping where they go, ensuring they have safe places to rest, and removing obstacles—working across borders and seasons like a single living system.

title: Protecting Carbon Hidden in Coastal Waters
tension: Carbon accounting (static stock measurement) vs. carbon stewardship (living cycle governance)
summary: Map and protect mangroves and seagrass that store vast carbon, while ensuring coastal communities benefit from conservation efforts.

title: Protecting Commons from Legal Risk
tension: Stewards need legal protection from personal liability to make decisions boldly, yet commons need enforceable accountability to prevent breach and negligence.
summary: Establish liability limits and legal structures that shield community assets from seizure while giving commons legal standing to defend themselves in court.

title: Protecting Everyone's Profit
tension: Adaptive pricing and growth vs. systemic profitability integrity
summary: A system that watches profit margins across your entire business, catches problems early, and makes sure everyone involved stays financially healthy.

title: Protecting Focus as Shared Resource
tension: Continuous interruption & fragmented attention vs. Protected focus & rhythmic cognitive cycles
summary: Design work rhythms that batch similar tasks, shield deep focus time, and expose the real cost of switching between them—so teams can sustain their thinking capacity together.

title: Protecting Heritage as Neighborhoods Change
tension: Erasure (algorithmic, economic, abstractive) vs. Rooting (scaled, embodied, collectively stewarded)
summary: Use targeted interventions at neighborhood scale to preserve cultural sites and communities from algorithmic bias and displacement pressures.

title: Protecting Informal Workers from Heat & Health Risks
tension: Worker health protection vs. informal economy fragmentation: individual workers lack power to negotiate safety; employers face no accountability; health systems remain disconnected from workplace realities.
